description:
Abstract

 Recently, a number of papers have addressed the use of pedigrees in the study of wild populations, highlighting the value of pedigrees in conservation management. We used pedigrees to study the horses (Equus caballus) of Assateague Island National Seashore, Maryland, USA, one of a small number of free-ranging animal populations that have been the subject of long-term studies. This population grew from 28 in 1968 to 175 in 2001, causing negative impacts on the island ecosystem. To minimize these effects, an immunocontraception program was instituted, and horse numbers are slowly decreasing. However, there is concern that this program may negatively affect the genetic health of the herd. We found that although mitochondrial DNA diversity is low, nuclear diversity is comparable to that of established breeds. Using genetic data, we verified and amended maternal pedigrees that had been primarily based on behavioral data and inferred paternity using genetic data along with National Park Service records of the historic ranges of males. The resulting pedigrees enabled us to examine demography, founder contributions, rates of inbreeding and loss of diversity over recent generations, as well as the level of kinship among horses. We then evaluated the strategy of removing individuals (using nonlethal means) with the highest mean kinship values. Although the removal strategy increased the retained diversity of founders and decreased average kinship between individuals, it disproportionately impacted sizes of the youngest age classes. Our results suggest that a combined strategy of controlled breeding and immunocontraception would be more effective than removing individuals with high mean kinships in preserving the long-term health and viability of the herd.
title: Pedigrees and the Study of Wild Populations: The Horses of Assateague Island National Seashore

title: The Zimmerman Formula: Derivation and Testable Predictions

description:
We present a novel, independent measurement of the Hubble constant H₀ using the MOND acceleration scale a₀ measured from galaxy rotation curves.                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                        
  METHOD: From the Zimmerman Formula a₀ = cH₀/5.79 (where 5.79 = 2√(8π/3) is derived from the Friedmann equation), we obtain H₀ = 5.79 ×  a₀ / c.                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                        
  INPUT: a₀ = (1.20 ± 0.02) × 10⁻¹⁰ m/s² from the Radial Acceleration Relation (McGaugh et al. 2016, SPARC database, 175+ galaxies).    
                                                                                                                                        
  RESULT: H₀ = 71.5 ± 1.2 km/s/Mpc                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                        
  This value lies between Planck (67.4) and SH0ES (73.0), with 3.2σ tension with Planck and 0.9σ agreement with SH0ES. Best agreement is with GW170817 standard siren (70.0, only 0.1σ difference).                                                                           
                                                                                                                                        
  INDEPENDENCE: Uses neither CMB physics nor the astronomical distance ladder — relies solely on galaxy kinematics.                                                                                                                                                       
  VERIFICATION: The formula is empirically validated — using Planck's ρ_c, the formula predicts a₀ = 1.19 × 10⁻¹⁰ m/s², matching observations within <1%.

title: The Hubble Constant from Galaxy Dynamics: An Independent Measurement Using the MOND Acceleration Scale

description:
We present a testable prediction: if the MOND acceleration scale a₀ is connected to cosmological density (a₀ ∝ √ρ_c), then a₀ must evolve with redshift as a₀(z) = a₀(0) × E(z), where E(z) = √(Ω_m(1+z)³ + Ω_Λ).                                                     
                                                                                                                                        
  KEY PREDICTION: At z = 10, a₀ was ~20× higher than today.                                                                             
                                                                                                                                        
  TEST: We compare this prediction against JWST kinematic data from 7 galaxies at z = 5.5-10.6 (JADES + GN-z11):                        
  • Evolving a₀: χ² = 4.4                                                                                                               
  • Constant a₀: χ² = 7.8                                                                                                               
  • Improvement: 1.8×                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                        
  IMPORTANT: This is a genuine, falsifiable prediction — NOT a fit. The evolution E(z) comes directly from Planck cosmology. If future observations show a₀(z) = constant, this framework is falsified.                                                                      
                                                                                                                                        
  SCOPE: We do NOT claim to derive the coefficient relating a₀ to ρ_c (that is empirically determined). We DO claim that IF a₀ ∝ √ρ_c, THEN the evolution follows mathematically and can be tested.

title: Redshift Evolution of the MOND Acceleration Scale: A Testable Prediction

description:
We report that five independent cosmological quantities share relationships involving the geometric factor 2√(8π/3) = 5.7888, arising from the Friedmann equation through ρc = 3H²/(8πG):                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                
  1. MOND acceleration: a₀ = cH₀/2√(8π/3) — 0.8% error                                                                                          
  2. Dark energy ratio: Ω_Λ/Ω_m = √(3π/2) — 0.04% error                                                                                         
  3. Optical depth: τ = Ω_m/2√(8π/3) — 0.12% error                                                                                              
  4. CMB/Structure: T_CMB/f_σ8 = 2√(8π/3) — 0.04% error                                                                                         
  5. Quantum (Unruh): λ_U/L_H ≈ 2√(8π/3) — ~2% error                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                

All values from Planck 2018, SPARC, COBE/FIRAS. Four sub-0.15% matches with the SAME geometric factor yields P ~ 10⁻¹² against coincidence.   
                                                                                                                                                

Key finding: The factor 8π/3 from Einstein's field equations propagates through galaxy dynamics, dark energy, reionization, structure growth, and quantum effects.                                                                                                                          

Testable prediction: Ω_m = 1/(1 + √(3π/2)) = 0.31538 exactly.

title: The Friedmann Geometric Factor: Five Cosmological Relationships

description:
We report the discovery that eleven independent cosmological and physical quantities share relationships involving the geometric factor 2√(8π/3) = 5.7888, which arises from the Friedmann equations through the critical density ρc = 3H²/(8πG).

  • Galaxy dynamics (MOND acceleration scale)                                                                                                  
  • Dark energy abundance

  • BAO sound horizon                                                                                                                           
  • Primordial fluctuations                                                                                                                     
  • CMB temperature

  2. Ω_Λ/Ω_m = √(3π/2) (0.04% error) - Dark energy ratio                                                                                        
  3. τ = Ω_m/Z (0.12% error) - Optical depth

  5. log₁₀(r_drag) = √(3π/2) (0.15% error) - BAO scale

The theory is anchored by the fundamental geometric constant Z² = 32π/3 ≈ 33.51, which is strictly derived as the Atiyah-Patodi-Singer (APS) eta invariant of the 3D internal orbifold. Version 11.1.0 provides a mathematically complete action principle that derives 53+ fundamental parameters with zero free inputs.

PROVEN MATHEMATICAL THEOREMS

APS Eta Theorem (v11.1.0): Utilizing the Brüning-Seeley theorem, we prove that each of the 8 fixed-point singularities contributes a spectral quantum of 4π/3 (unit 3-ball volume), yielding the definitive framework constant Z² = 32π/3.

Cube Uniqueness: We prove the cube is the unique Platonic solid capable of tessellating 3D Euclidean space, establishing the fundamental lattice of the vacuum.

Three Generations: We derive exactly three independent fermion families from the first Betti number of the 3-torus (b₁(T³) = 3) and the Atiyah-Singer index theorem.

Unique Gauge Partition: Utilizing Wilson's Theorem and Lie Algebra classification, we prove that the 12 degrees of freedom on the cubic lattice uniquely partition into the 8+3+1 structure of the Standard Model (su(3) ⊕ su(2) ⊕ u(1)).

THE FOUR PILLARS (FULLY DERIVED)

Fine Structure Constant: α⁻¹ = 4Z² + 3 ≈ 137.041. A refined two-loop iterative solution achieves a precision of 0.000002% compared to CODATA 2022.

Higgs Sector: We derive the Higgs quartic coupling λ = 13/(32π) = 0.1293 from topological mode counting, predicting a Higgs mass of 125.22 GeV (0.03% error).

Neutrino Sector: The T³/Z₂ topology strictly requires neutrinos to be Majorana particles, deriving a mass splitting ratio Δm²₃₁/Δm²₂₁ = Z² (2.8% error).

Strong Coupling: αs = 4/Z² ≈ 0.119. Derived via the propagation/confinement reciprocity principle, yielding an exact Abelian/Non-Abelian duality.

COSMOLOGICAL DYNAMICS

CDE Tracking Attractor: Version 11.1.0 replaces static scaling with a Coupled Dark Energy (CDE) dynamical model. We prove that a tracking attractor forces the density ratio ΩΛ/Ωm → 13/6, explaining the coincidence problem while respecting Friedmann expansion.

Inflationary Tensor Ratio: We derive a precise tensor-to-scalar ratio r = 1/(2Z²) ≈ 0.0149, testable at 15σ by the upcoming CMB-S4 survey.

Birefringence Defense: The framework maintains a prediction of zero cosmic birefringence (β = 0°) due to vacuum symmetry, identifying the current 4.9σ tension as a potential foreground systematic.
title: The Z² Unified Framework: A Topological Approach to Fundamental Physics

description:
The MOND acceleration scale as the cosmic dynamical acceleration: a scaling–MOND cosmology and its bridges to the dark sector

We examine the proposal that the Milgromian acceleration scale is the cosmic dynamical acceleration, a₀ = c²√(Gρ_c) = cH(z)/Z with Z = 2√(8π/3) ≈ 5.789. The evolving‑scale hypothesis itself is Milgrom's (2014); our contribution is an explicit covariant realization of it and a proof of its CMB‑safety. Algebraically a₀ = cH/Z re‑expresses the long‑known coincidence a₀ ≈ cH₀ through the Friedmann relation; its coefficient‑free consequence is that the scale evolves, a₀(z) = a₀(0) E(z). Fitting a₀ ∝ E(z)^p to the recent compilation (SPARC; Vărăşteanu 2025; MUSE–DARK III 2026) gives p = 0.80 ± 0.17; constant a₀ is excluded at 5σ in the nominal fit, but a jackknife and an inter‑method systematic (the 1.7σ discrepancy between the two near‑coincident local anchors) reduce this to ≈ 2σ, so we treat the trend as a suggestive hint, not a detection. Working from the Aether–Scalar–Tensor (AeST) action we promote the scale to the aether expansion, a₀ = cθ/(3Z), and show by order‑counting—reinforced by the identity δq⁰⁰ = 0 that survives perturbing the aether itself—that a₀ is absent from the linear cosmological perturbations; the running therefore leaves the linear CMB and P(k) exactly invariant, which we confirm by direct integration of the Einstein–Boltzmann system (r_s = 144.3 Mpc, ℓ_A = 301.7). We are explicit about the boundaries: the O(1) coefficient Z is a posit; the Standard‑Model constants do not follow; and the apparent‑a₀ evolution is itself reproduced by ΛCDM hydrodynamic simulations, so the amplitude alone does not discriminate. The one prediction that does—a redshift‑weakening external field effect, η = g_ext/a₀(z) ∝ 1/E(z), distinct from both ΛCDM and constant‑a₀ MOND—is forecast to require a dedicated z ≳ 4 campaign.
title: Scaling MOND with Z

description: The acceleration scale a0 = 9.36e-11 m/s^2 that governs galaxy dynamics is proposed to be set by the cosmological constant: a0 = c^2 sqrt(Lambda/32pi) = (c/2) sqrt(G rho_Lambda) = c H_Lambda / Z, Z = sqrt(32pi/3) = 5.789, on the dark-energy density alone. The paper assembles the empirical confrontation (RAR, BTFR and deep-MOND relations agree to 8% at this a0; the rising a0 ~ cH rival is excluded; the LCDM-impossible External Field Effect leans the predicted way) and the theoretical foundation (the deep-MOND shape is derived = Milgrom de Sitter-Unruh modified inertia; a0's existence is volume-law-free; the galaxy-scale sign is forced by a computed DSSYK kernel that also predicts the cluster failure; the value of Lambda is welded to a0 as one Cohen-Kaplan-Nelson seesaw; the evolving dark energy is string-swampland-compatible where LCDM is forbidden). Limits stated plainly: the O(1) coefficient is a posit, the covariant completion is unwritten, and this is a theory of gravity and the dark sector, not a theory of everything. The distinctive falsifiable prediction is a0(z=3) = 0.74 a0(0), testable with ELT-class spectroscopy.
title: The Zimmerman Theory of Gravity

description: A falsification-map whitepaper for the acceleration scale a₀ = c²√(Λ/32π) ≈ 9.36×10⁻¹¹ m/s², anchoring galactic dynamics to the cosmological constant. The program tests the kernel against SPARC rotation curves, an independent 181k-lens re-measurement of the weak-lensing RAR, wide binaries, the solar system, and the CMB — recording kills and survivals with equal weight under pre-registered, convention-audited methods. Contents: a nine-link derivation chain from Λ to the named effective law; exact no-go theorems (no passive medium — linear or nonlinear — produces the modified-inertia channel; de Sitter Källén–Lehmann positivity excludes every invariant carrier; local and history-keyed lensing-slip carriers are excluded by the keying and static-equivalence theorems); a four-sector candidate action with exactly one underived number; and the Link-5 mechanism calculation: an explicit pump profile that passes every physical gate, together with a generation-obstruction theorem showing the profile's locked cube-root structure must originate upstream — the open generator question. The paper claims no completed theory: Z = √(32π/3) remains data-selected, the lensing carrier unrealized, the quantum gate open. Approximately twenty dated falsifiable predictions are registered. All results carry commit-hash provenance to the public repository.
title: The Λ-Anchored Acceleration Scale a₀ = c²√(Λ/32π): A Completed Falsification Map, Exact No-Go Results, and the Specification of the Unique Surviving Object

description: An affirmative case for identifying the galactic acceleration scale with the cosmological constant, a0 = c^2*sqrt(Lambda/32pi) = 9.36e-11 m/s^2. On real SPARC galaxy data the framework reproduces the radial-acceleration relation (0.105 dex), the baryonic Tully-Fisher relation (slope 3.87), and Renzo's rule (galaxy-specific, permutation p~0) with no per-galaxy freedom, and explains the a0-Lambda coincidence that LCDM cannot. LCDM's standing is examined both ways: its genuine cracks (the cosmological-constant problem, the undetected dark-matter particle, the ~5sigma Hubble tension, DESI evolving dark energy, the ~5sigma cosmic-dipole challenge to the cosmological principle) and the two clean LCDM-impossible tests (the external field effect and wide binaries) that Gaia DR4 will adjudicate. Open problems are stated explicitly (the coefficient Z underived; clusters and the CMB 3rd peak conceded; a0(z) decline unconfirmed). Every load-bearing number is recomputed on real data. Technical edition.
title: The Cosmological Constant Sets the Galaxy Acceleration Scale: An Affirmative Case for a0 = c^2 sqrt(Lambda/32pi)

description: A plain-language but quantitative explanation, for a numerate reader with no physics background, of why galaxies spin faster than their visible mass allows, and of a one-number formula a0 = c^2*sqrt(Lambda/32pi) that resolves it by deriving the galactic acceleration threshold from the cosmological constant. Covers the radial-acceleration relation, the baryonic Tully-Fisher relation, a permutation test of Renzo's rule, the genuine cracks in LCDM (including the ~5sigma cosmic dipole), the two decisive upcoming tests, and an explicit list of what is not yet established. Companion to the technical paper.
title: Why Galaxies Spin Too Fast: A One-Number Formula That Explains It

description: A children's explainer (about a 5th-grade reading level) of why the stars at the edge of a galaxy move too fast for the matter we can see, the two ideas that try to explain it (invisible dark matter versus a small change to gravity when it is very weak), and how the special 'weakness' number can be computed from how fast the whole universe is expanding. Honest about what is not yet known. Companion to the technical and plain-language editions.
title: Why Do the Stars at the Edge of a Galaxy Go So Fast? A Galaxy Mystery Explained for Kids

description: An essay, written from the chair of a modified-gravity rival, arguing that the decades-long dark-matter search was not wasted: it built the precision measurement infrastructure that makes the framework a0 = c^2*sqrt(Lambda/32pi) = 9.36e-11 m/s^2 a decidable scientific claim rather than a coincidence, and on galaxy scales rewards its parsimony. Instrument by instrument: the rotation-curve enterprise culminating in SPARC measured the radial-acceleration relation (g_dagger=1.20e-10, 0.13 dex) and the slope-4 baryonic Tully-Fisher relation that the framework reproduces with one acceleration scale and zero per-galaxy freedom; weak-lensing surveys (KiDS/DES/HSC/Euclid) built an independent test two decades deeper; X-ray cluster surveys (eROSITA/eRASS1, Bulbul+2024) let the framework state its heaviest loss (~2x missing cluster mass) to the decimal; the CMB program (Planck) measured the cosmological constant Lambda = 3*Omega_Lambda*H0^2/c^2 that is the literal input the framework's formula consumes; forty years of direct-detection nulls (LZ 2024) keep a no-new-particle account scientifically live; and Gaia, built to weigh the dark halo, now hosts the two clean tests (wide binaries and the external field effect) that Gaia DR4 (Dec 2026) will adjudicate. The framework's standing losses (clusters, the CMB third peak, the weak-lensing morphology split) and the non-diagnostic, shared-with-MOND nature of its SPARC success are stated straight. Both-ways honesty throughout.
title: The Search Was Never Wasted: How the Hunt for Dark Matter Built the Measurements That Make a0 = c^2 sqrt(Lambda/32pi) a Decidable Claim

description: Gravitational lensing is routinely presented as direct, model-independent evidence for particle dark matter. This paper shows that within a framework in which the modified-dynamics acceleration scale is set by the cosmological constant, a0 = c^2 sqrt(Lambda/32pi) = 9.36e-11 m/s^2, realised covariantly by the Aether-Scalar-Tensor (AeST) theory, this evidentiary status collapses: AeST has no gravitational slip (the two weak-field potentials are equal, Phi=Psi), so the lensing mass equals the dynamical mass for any source. Four standard lensing-for-dark-matter arguments (the Bullet cluster offset, cluster strong+weak lensing masses, the galaxy-galaxy-lensing radial acceleration relation, and strong-lens Einstein radii) therefore reduce to a single statement -- that clusters carry a residual between dynamical and baryonic mass -- rather than four independent proofs. The acceleration-scale footing of the measurements is audited (cluster lensing masses are pure GR+dark-matter deductions with no a0; the framework uses its own least-favourable a0). Reported both ways: the galaxy-galaxy-lensing relation passes; the cluster residual and the CMB third peak remain genuinely independent, conceded losses; the 8.6-9.2 sigma weak-lensing morphology split is now contested by a re-analysis of the same data.
title: Gravitational lensing is not independent evidence for dark matter: the no-slip identity in a cosmological-constant acceleration-scale framework

description: The de Sitter-MOND framework ties the galactic acceleration scale to the dark-energy density, a0 = c^2 sqrt(Lambda/32pi) = (c/2) sqrt(G rho_DE). Promoted across cosmic time this becomes a parameter-free SHAPE prediction, a0(z)/a0(0) = sqrt(rho_DE(z)/rho_DE(0)) -- both the coefficient and the MOND interpolation function cancel in the ratio, so the evolution of a0 is fixed entirely by the dark-energy equation of state w(z), with no remaining freedom. (The sqrt(rho_DE) scaling itself is not novel -- it appears in Limbach, Psaltis & Ozel 2008 -- but the framework promotes it to a forced relation and the data now make it sharp.) DESI DR2's measured time-evolving dark energy (w0 ~ -0.75, wa ~ -0.86) drives a0(z) along a distinctive NON-MONOTONIC track: a +6% rise to a peak at z ~ 0.41, precisely the phantom-divide crossing where w(z) = -1, then a decline to a0(z=3) ~ 0.74 a0(0). The cleanest measurable signature is the SIGN of the high-z deep-MOND baryonic Tully-Fisher offset: the framework predicts rotation velocities 0.033 dex (-7.3% in V) below the local relation at z=3, where standard fixed-a0 MOND sits on it and the rival rising sqrt(rho_total) reading (already disfavored by Milgrom 2017 / RC100 / cluster offsets) sits +0.166 dex above. We argue this is a near-term falsification test that LCDM STRUCTURALLY CANNOT TAKE -- cold dark matter has no acceleration scale to evolve -- while stating plainly that it is NON-DIAGNOSTIC TODAY: the framework is hostage to a DESI result it cannot influence, dissolves to ordinary fixed-a0 MOND if w reverts to -1 (dissolution, not falsification), and the present a0(z) data (including MUSE-DARK III, Ciocan 2026, whose raw rising signal de-systematizes to consistent-with-zero through the same LCDM baryon-fraction degeneracy that makes all current a0(z) inferences non-diagnostic) are systematics-limited in both directions. The verdict arrives on two independent axes: DESI DR3 / DESI-final (w(z), ~2026-27, the gate) and high-z resolved kinematics (ALMA BTFR-offset sign ~2028-30; ELT/HARMONI clean multi-redshift tracking, early-mid 2030s). Kill conditions are stated explicitly. Honesty markers: the value a0(0) is NOT derived (one free normalization kappa=1/2; only the shape is predicted); the w0wa inputs carry DESI's uncertainties and vary across SNe compilations; the covariant lensing sector remains phenomenological as in all relativistic-MOND theories. This is a falsifiable prediction of a gravity/dark-sector effective theory -- not a proven replacement for dark matter, and not a theory of everything yet, as frustrating as it may be.
title: Dark Energy Sets the Galaxy Acceleration Scale: A Parameter-Free a0(z) Test LCDM Cannot Take

description: The de Sitter-MOND framework writes the galactic acceleration scale as a0 = c^2 sqrt(Lambda/32pi) = kappa c sqrt(G rho_DE), and the FORM a0 ~ c^2 sqrt(Lambda) together with the gravitational kernel sqrt(8pi/3) (including the half-integer power of pi) are forced. This paper asks whether the single residual coefficient kappa=1/2 is forced or free, and proves a sharp result: kappa is the framework's lone free number, and it is PROVABLY UNFORCEABLE by the three standard consistency conditions -- ghost-freedom, unitarity, and a holographic / degree-of-freedom bound -- each failing for a structurally distinct, machine-verified reason. (i) Ghost-freedom is blind to kappa because kappa is the overall normalization of a phi_- -linear, degree-1-homogeneous action: the equation of motion divides cleanly by it and every no-ghost/stability inequality and sound speed is normalization-invariant. (ii) Unitarity (Schwinger-Keldysh/in-in positivity) reaches only signs, causality, and noise/dissipation ratios with a temperature -- never an absolute scale -- and for the conservative even kernel the fluctuation-dissipation relation is vacuous. (iii) Holography reaches only the scale cH (the unique hbar-free acceleration); the sole dimensionless group G hbar H^2/c^5 ~ 1/S_dS ~ 1e-122 is hbar-laden and cancels classically, and CKN/Bousso/de Sitter-equipartition are inequalities saturated with a free O(1) whose fixing to the target IS choosing kappa (circular). The paper then identifies what kappa IS: the framework coefficient sqrt(2/Z)=(3/8pi)^(1/4)=0.58779 (Z=sqrt(32pi/3)) is PURE GEOMETRY, carrying no degree-of-freedom, thermal, or entropy content, and it equals exactly the single-degree-of-freedom (g_*=1) limit of the Cohen-Kaplan-Nelson (CKN) UV-IR bound -- the machine-exact geometric identity 3/8pi = (Schwarzschild 1/2)/(ball 4pi/3). An honest count of the Standard Model degrees of freedom (g_*=106.75) gives a CKN coefficient of ~0.18-0.41 (energy version, scaling as g_*^(-1/4)) to ~0.31-0.41 (entropy version, g_*^(-1/3)) -- never within 5% of the framework value; a constant and a strictly-decreasing function of g_* coincide only at one tuned non-SM root (g_*~3-25), so demanding agreement is circular. kappa is therefore GEOMETRIC, not microscopic. The framework is a PROVABLY one-parameter theory of gravity and the dark sector -- one knob, irreducible and geometric -- versus LCDM's six parameters plus an undetected particle. The paper states plainly what this does and does NOT establish, both ways: it fixes the parameter economy and the irreducibility of the lone number (with anti-circularity held: kappa kept symbolic, the value 1/2 and the 8pi density route appear only in the post-hoc locating map, and the g_*=1 identity fell out of an independent derivation); it does NOT derive a0's value (the dS-Unruh temperature route's natural scale is 2cH_Lambda, ~12x too large, and the empirical a0 requires the density route plus the kappa=1/2 posit), it does NOT make the sector zero-parameter, and it does NOT confirm the framework against LCDM (a theory can be maximally economical and still wrong; that verdict belongs to the data). All identities are machine-verified and reproducible. This is a structural result for a falsifiable theory of gravity and the dark sector -- not a proven replacement for dark matter, and not a theory of everything yet, as frustrating as it may be.
title: A Provably One-Parameter Theory of Gravity and the Dark Sector: the de Sitter-MOND Coefficient kappa=1/2 Is Unforceable Geometry

description: The Aether-Scalar-Tensor theory (AeST) of Skordis and Złośnik (2021) is the relativistic completion of MOND that fits the full Planck CMB power spectrum (third acoustic peak included) while reproducing the galaxy-scale radial acceleration relation. It is commonly criticised on three grounds: (i) its scalar kinetic function K(Q)=mu^2(Q-1)^2 is postulated; (ii) its preferred (aether) frame is postulated; and (iii) its MOND acceleration scale a0 is fitted, not derived. We argue that on every count Skordis and Złośnik were right, and that the framework a0 = c^2 sqrt(Lambda/32pi) = (c/2) sqrt(G rho_DE) = cH_Lambda/Z (with Z = sqrt(32pi/3) = 5.7888) supplies precisely the physical motivation those three postulates were missing, without altering a single one of AeST's successful predictions. The acceleration scale is tied to the cosmological constant through a de Sitter-Unruh effective temperature, fixing a0 = 9.36e-11 m/s^2 to within the radial-acceleration-relation band; the preferred frame is named by the de Sitter vacuum (the cosmic rest frame where the Gibbons-Hawking floor is isotropic); and the K(Q) ghost condensate is shown to be internally healthy -- energy-positivity of the cold a^-3 dust forces the shift-charge sign(I0)>0 onto the gradient-stable branch, and the boost-free infrared positivity/causality bounds of Grall-Melville (2021) and Serra-Trombetta (2024) -- the latter written at Skordis's own institute (CEICO Prague) -- are cleared. We are scrupulously two-sided: the framework derives no number (a0's coefficient kappa, the kinetic-term origin, and the dark-sector amplitude all remain free or postulated, exactly as in AeST); the positivity result is a saturation-pass that transmits no new constraint (the real Blanchet-Skordis quadratic action has a vanishing k^4 coefficient); the cluster-core deficit is shared identically with AeST (the framework's modified-inertia residual equals AeST's modified-gravity residual to machine precision, and both undershoot the CLASH and XLSSC 122 cores); and three independent attempts to derive the kinetic term from Lambda (de Sitter-Unruh vacuum induction, the Mersini-Houghton forcing theorem, and Oda's GR-from-Lambda ghost-condensation mechanism) all return NOT-FORCED, with the SO(4,1) gate proven group-theoretically (the defining representation of so(4,1) is irreducible, so the de Sitter vacuum admits no invariant timelike vector). The net is a vindication, not a replacement: AeST is sound, well-founded, and -- read as modified inertia with a0 set by Lambda -- even better-motivated than its authors claimed. We close with the live falsifiable tests (Gaia DR4 wide binaries ~December 2026, the s^TX Lorentz-violation dipole, the evolving-a0 Tully-Fisher offset, and the modified-inertia cluster sigma-spread). This is a synthesis/position paper, not a discovery paper and not a claim of a theory of everything: it presents a re-reading of AeST's acceleration scale and a consistency demonstration, with all quantitative claims reproduced by 60 committed Python scripts (all exit 0) at https://github.com/carlzimmerman/zimmerman-formula. Quarantine note: a0, Z, kappa, and the dark-sector amplitude I0 are never asserted to be derived.
title: Why Skordis and Złośnik Were Right: The MOND Acceleration Scale as a de Sitter-Unruh Manifestation of the Cosmological Constant

description: MOND and its relativistic completions reproduce galaxy rotation curves with one acceleration scale a0 but leave a factor-~2 missing-mass residual in galaxy-cluster cores (Sanders 1999, 2003), shared across the whole relativistic-MOND family. We ask whether this residual is explained WITHIN the de Sitter-MOND framework (a0 = c^2 sqrt(Lambda/32pi) = cH_Lambda/Z, Z = sqrt(32pi/3) = 5.7888, a0 = 9.36e-11 m/s^2), whose dark sector is the Aether-Scalar-Tensor (AeST) ghost-condensate of Skordis & Zlosnik (2021): a cold, w=0, rho~a^-3 MODE of the gravity field, not a new particle. We report a clean two-sided result. (i) The abundance is NOT the problem: the AeST shift-symmetric Q-mode carries Omega_dm worth of cold density, which at the cosmic dark-to-baryon ratio supplies ~7.0e14 Msun inside R500 against the ~4.79e14 a factor-2 cluster requires -- a ratio of 1.46, with ZERO mass tuning. The framework's dark sector HAS the cluster mass. (ii) But it cannot deploy that mass galaxy-safely: the Q-mode is sound-speed-zero (c_s^2 -> 0) sub-horizon -- the very property that lets AeST fit the Planck third acoustic peak -- so its Jeans length vanishes and growth is gated only by the mass term rho > mu^2/4piG. Galaxy disks and cluster cores both exceed this by ~10^13, AND the galaxy disk is ~3.7x DENSER than the cluster core: the density ordering runs BACKWARDS, so any field that clumps in cluster cores clumps MORE in galaxies. Injecting the required density into a fiducial disk shifts the radial-acceleration relation by +0.12 to +0.23 dex against a 0.11-0.14 dex scatter floor -- re-introducing the cuspy-halo scatter MOND was built to remove. No acceleration gate evades this: a0 is absent from the AeST linear perturbations (Bridge-1), so the dust grows CDM-identically. The conclusion is a no-go, stated symmetrically: the residual IS the framework's own dark sector doing a cold-dark-matter job -- that is the explanation -- but in the two clean field limits the sector either over-fills clusters and breaks galaxies, or stays galaxy-safe and fills only ~17-20% of the core. description: Tidal dwarf galaxies (TDGs) -- condensations formed from tidal debris pulled from a progenitor disc during a galaxy interaction -- are the classic sign-flip test between dark matter and modified dynamics: in LCDM they are born devoid of non-baryonic dark matter and should be Newtonian (Mdyn/Mbar ~ 1), while in INSTANTANEOUS modified dynamics (modified gravity AQUAL/QUMOND, or short-memory modified inertia) they sit deep in the low-acceleration regime (current g_bar/a0 = 0.015-0.073; Lelli et al. 2015) and should show a large boost (nu ~ 6, Mdyn/Mbar ~ 4-8). The best HI kinematics (Lelli et al. 2015, six TDGs around NGC 5291 and NGC 7252 plus VCC 2062) instead give Mdyn/Mbar = 0.9-1.5: near-Newtonian. Instantaneous modified dynamics over-predicts the rotation velocities even with the external-field effect, at roughly 2-3 sigma per NGC 5291 object (the lower framework a0 = 9.355e-11 vs the standard 1.2e-10 helps by only ~6%). This paper reads the same data through the de Sitter-Unruh MODIFIED-INERTIA framework, using its OWN interpolation nu(y) = sqrt(1+1/y), its own footings (canonical a0 = 9.355e-11 = cH_Lambda/Z / alt 1.1305e-10, both carried), and its COMMITTED memory kernel tau_mem = 2Z/H_Lambda = 203 Gyr (the same kernel used in the relational sigma-spread and SHLEM analyses). Because TDG ages (~0.36 Gyr) are minute compared with tau_mem, the debris gas has NOT relaxed to its current deep-regime inertia; its effective inertia is dominated by the ~10-13 Gyr it spent at higher acceleration in the progenitor disc. Averaging the RESPONSE nu the way the framework's own sigma-spread analysis does (a Jensen gap over the convex nu, with residence-time weight w ~ 0.36/13.8 ~ 2.6% for the recent low-acceleration epoch, since the committed kernel is power-law/non-saturating), a plausible outer-disc history (y_hist ~ 0.5-2) gives nu_eff ~ 1.4-1.9, i.e. Mdyn/Mbar ~ 1.4-1.9. This RESOLVES the gross factor-~4 instantaneous over-prediction (nu ~ 6 -> ~1.5) but lands at the HIGH EDGE of, and mildly above, the observed range (over-predicting the older, lower-mass NGC 7252/VCC by a few tenths, within their +/-0.6 errors) -- a consistency, not a bullseye. The freeze is defended by the committed formalism, not asserted: the field-theory closure carries a single scale a0 and rejects any orbital-time (dynamical) relaxation corner as a new scale absent from the action, so the 203-Gyr memory is orbit-independent and the debris does not re-equilibrate on a galaxy dynamical time. HONEST SCOPE, stated prominently BOTH WAYS: (GAIN) TDGs become a candidate HISTORY-DEPENDENCE discriminator -- instantaneous modified dynamics is disfavored at ~2-3 sigma while long-memory modified inertia and LCDM both survive; a new member of the framework's history-dependence family (with the sigma-spread and SHLEM), and the first with data at least compatible with the memory-kernel direction. (COST, up front) under the long-memory reading the framework predicts the SAME near-Newtonian TDGs as LCDM, so the classic sign-flip discriminator against dark matter DISSOLVES for this framework -- this paper must NOT be read as 'TDGs show no dark matter' or as confirmation of the framework. (CAVEAT 1) Lelli's own non-equilibrium escape (TDG orbital times >> ages -> discs may be unsettled -> Vcirc underestimates the potential) ALSO rescues instantaneous MOND, so 'long-memory MI' and 'instantaneous MOND + non-equilibrium' are degenerate on current data. (CAVEAT 2) the nu_eff mapping is kernel-hostage: the outer-disc history y_hist is assumed (least-bound-gas prior skews it low, nu_eff high), and the averaging rule is unpinned (response-averaging gives 1.4-1.9, the generic acceleration-averaging shortcut gives a lower, more favorable 1.2-1.7 -- a ~20-30% swing). (CAVEAT 3, self-correction on the record) the first pass of this analysis wrongly reported a ~2-3 sigma tension AGAINST the framework by applying the instantaneous (standard-lens) prediction to a theory that commits to a 203-Gyr kernel; that adverse verdict is retracted and re-scoped to instantaneous modified gravity and short-memory inertia. HONEST WARNING on the forecast: the touted age-vs-discrepancy gradient (older TDGs -> more boost) runs the WRONG way in the present sample (older NGC 7252 has LOWER Mdyn/Mbar than younger NGC 5291), within errors but not supporting evidence. The values of a0, Z, and the map from the 203-Gyr history average to nu_eff remain posited or estimated, not derived. Phys. 229, 384); the interpolation kernel is Milgrom 1999 (PLA 253:273); the TDG non-equilibrium caution is Lelli 2015 / Kroupa. description:
Preprint of a manuscript submitted to Physical Review D (Regular Article). This deposit exists to timestamp the result and to carry the reproducibility scripts; it is not a journal publication.

The result, in one line. The acceleration scale that organizes galactic rotation curves admits the exact closed form

a0 = ½ c √(G ρΛ) = c2 √(Λ/32π) = cHΛ/√(32π/3)

The three forms are algebraically identical, and the reduction cancels every factor of π and the 3. With the Planck 2018 ρΛ this evaluates to 9.43×10-11 m s-2, which is 0.70% from the value 9.36×10-11 m s-2 obtained by fitting the 175 SPARC rotation curves at a stellar mass-to-light ratio Υ[3.6] = 0.70 (residual scatter 0.108 dex; Υ = 0.70 lies inside the 0.5-0.8 range expected for Spitzer 3.6 µm populations). The expression is parameter-free apart from the rational coefficient ½.

What is NOT claimed, stated up front because it bounds the result.

  • The coefficient ½ is fitted, not derived. An attempt to force it from ghost-freedom, unitarity and a holographic degree-of-freedom count is reported as having failed.
  • The interpolating function used is identical to Eq. (9) of Milgrom, Phys. Lett. A 253, 273 (1999) — not a variant of it. That same paper derives a0 = 2cHΛ, a factor 11.58 larger, so the de Sitter-Unruh route does not leave the coefficient open: it predicts one and misses the measured scale by an order of magnitude. The present contribution is a renormalization of that coefficient to match data, not a new derivation.
  • The coefficient here is not observationally distinguishable from the empirical cHΛ/2π of Milgrom (2020): √(32π/3) = 5.789 against 2π = 6.283 differ by 7.9%, i.e. 0.018 dex in gobs, only 16% of the fit scatter. No claim of improved fit is made. The contribution is one of form.
  • √(32π/3) carries no geometric content; it is the unit conversion between HΛ and √(GρΛ) bookkeeping. Reading 32π/3 as a structure to be explained is an error the author has previously made and explicitly disavows here.
  • No claim is made regarding particle physics, the Standard Model, or unification. The author publicly withdrew earlier statements of that kind and does not restate them.

One falsifiable consequence. If a0 ∝ √ρΛ then a0(z)/a0(0) = (1+z)1.5(1+w0+wa) exp[-1.5 wa z/(1+z)], which is exactly constant for w = -1 and rises to a maximum before declining for the DESI-preferred w0 > -1, wa < 0 — in contrast to the monotonic rise predicted by a0 ∝ cH(z). A measured monotonic rise would exclude the relation. One reported determination of a rising a0(z) is recorded as a live tension, not as support.

Known tensions, handed over rather than left to be found. (i) Clusters: the same closure underpredicts cluster-scale accelerations, with a median discrepancy factor 2.33 at R500 on uncorrected eRASS1 masses and a lensing-inferred cluster scale 21.6× the value above; because this a0 is lower than the conventional one, the discrepancy is 13% worse here. (ii) Solar system: applied exactly, the closure leaves a constant residual a0/2 three orders above Earth-Mars ranging bounds; an interpolation with a faster Newtonian approach leaves a02/2g instead and reduces this by five orders at a cost of 0.003 dex in the SPARC fit. The word “exact” should not be attached to the closure. (iii) a0 and Υ are degenerate in the fit; nothing here determines a0 to better than the 7.9% separating it from cHΛ/2π.

Provenance. The relation was arrived at independently via three routes: an agentic automated-research harness (Karpathy, autoresearch) adapted by the author to search dimensional combinations of c, G, Λ and H0; symbolic regression in the spirit of AI Feynman (Udrescu & Tegmark, Sci. Adv. 6, eaay2631, 2020); and direct fitting to the SPARC compilation (Lelli, McGaugh & Schombert, AJ 152, 157, 2016). Routes 1-2 identified the form; route 3 fixed the coefficient. None constitutes a derivation, and a coefficient obtained by fitting remains fitted however it was found.

AI-assistance disclosure. Portions of the analysis, numerical verification and drafting were carried out with the assistance of a large language model (Anthropic Claude). The author directed the work, specified and reviewed every load-bearing calculation, and takes full responsibility including for any errors. No AI system satisfies the criteria for authorship and none is listed as an author. Several intermediate claims produced during the work were found to be incorrect and were withdrawn before this deposit.

Reproducibility. Every numerical claim is produced by a committed script that exits with a nonzero status if any internal consistency check fails. The verification script for this deposit is included.

description:
The MOND acceleration scale is numerically close to c H_Lambda, and the proposal that it is SET by the cosmological constant dates to Milgrom (1994, 1999). The relation's FORM is established; its dimensionless O(1) COEFFICIENT is not derived by any published argument, and the live proposals differ: Milgrom (1999) gives a0 = 2 c H_Lambda, Milgrom (2020) gives kappa = 1/2pi, and this author has used a0 = (1/2) c sqrt(G rho_Lambda), i.e. a0 = c H_Lambda / Z with Z = 2 sqrt(8 pi/3). That last value is FITTED, NOT DERIVED, and nothing in this paper changes that.

This paper is about what could change it. We prove a RELABELLING THEOREM: because Lambda = 8 pi G rho_Lambda/c^2 identically, G rho_Lambda and c^2 Lambda are the SAME scale up to the pure number 8 pi, so any combination of the two returns that scale times a power of 8 pi and cannot select a coefficient or exclude c H_Lambda. We then audit three constructions of the kind that naturally suggest themselves. All three fail: one on dimensions (its geometric mean is a frequency-squared, not an acceleration, and the charitable repair overshoots by exactly (8 pi)^(1/4)); one because its free parameter is merely relocated (for any inertia functional of the local de Sitter-Unruh temperature the crossover is q = 2 c1prime / f-prime(T_GH) = 2/r with r free, so an explicit admissible functional reaches kappa = 1/2 but only by trading one fitted number for another); and one on a sign that makes its central invariant imaginary in any homogeneous vacuum. Two of the three additionally attach their coefficient to a0 rather than to the FLOOR a0/2 that Milgrom's balance actually contains; having committed the same error ourselves, we record it as a systematic hazard.

Three results are constructive. (i) The theorem does NOT exclude a single-scale derivation: sqrt(G rho_Lambda) is pi-free while sqrt(8 pi G rho_Lambda/3) is not, so a construction taking rho_Lambda as its only input is untouched by the theorem and would automatically exclude c H_Lambda, being unable to manufacture the Friedmann 8 pi/3. (ii) No standard local rate supplies the required factor 1/4: over seven candidates the closest is sqrt(G rho/4 pi) at 12.84% away, wider than the 7.87% separating the two published coefficients, so there is no near miss. Since kappa is fitted, searching constructions until one reproduces 1/4 is reverse-engineering a fit, and any candidate must make an independent prediction. (iii) The choice of floor is OBSERVATIONALLY DECIDABLE and needs no new mechanism: a local response to the vacuum DENSITY gives a0 proportional to sqrt(rho_DE), exactly constant for w = -1 and blind to matter, whereas a horizon floor tracks c H(z) = c H_0 E(z), rising to 1.78, 3.01 and 4.54 times its present value at z = 1, 2, 3. The local reading is therefore the MORE falsifiable of the two, because it forbids the rising branch the horizon reading permits.

A by-product worth separating from the negative results: the detector-response calculation reproduces Deser and Levin's temperature sqrt(a^2+H^2)/2pi to 1e-15 to 1e-17 across three radii from a computed Unruh-DeWitt response on a non-rotating worldline, so the temperature Milgrom's balance POSITS is here obtained rather than assumed. Rotation breaks the KMS condition only at order (v/c)^2, falling short of the freedom needed for kappa = 1/2 by a factor 1.2e7, which makes the response route a null for the coefficient.

Phys. 229, 384 section II eq. 3 writes a_lambda = c^2 sqrt(Lambda/3); the interpolating function nu = sqrt(1+1/y) and the temperature balance are Milgrom 1999 Phys. Lett. description:
The MOND acceleration scale a0 is numerically close to c H_Lambda, and several authors have proposed that it is set by the cosmological constant. The relation's form is established (Milgrom 1994, 1999, 2020); its dimensionless O(1) coefficient is not derived by any published argument. This note reports two independent barriers to fixing it and quantifies both.

First, a theoretical barrier. We compute the Unruh-DeWitt response for a circular worldline in de Sitter space and extract the MOND crossover coefficient q defined by a0 = q c H_Lambda. Milgrom's (1999) balance uses a hyperbolic worldline and gives q = 2; a circular orbit is never hyperbolic, so that derivation is scope-limited to linear acceleration while galaxies are orbits. We find q = 2 exactly on orbits, for two independent reasons both forced by the identity A^2 h^2 - R^2 w^2 = 1: the short-time correlator depends only on a5^2 = a^2 + H^2, which holds for any worldline on the hyperboloid; and the full-response orbital correction is an a-independent rescaling (verified to 1e-16 over five decades in a/H) which cancels identically in the crossover ratio. The mechanism returns Milgrom's coefficient and cannot be made to yield a smaller one.

Second, an observational barrier that dissolves into a theoretical one. Profiling SPARC with the mass-to-light ratio free per galaxy, the preferred a0 spans 30.6% across five admissible interpolation shapes - nearly four times the 7.87% separating the two published coefficient proposals. We identify the mechanism: the likelihood anchors on a single deep acceleration (boost nu = 3.97, y = 0.06) where the five kernels agree to 1.14%; the knee is not the anchor and correcting there over-corrects by 3.4x. The spread is already diluted 5.5x by the sample's 1.57 decades of coverage in y, so more data at one acceleration cannot reduce it. But the kernels are not degenerate - after optimal a0 rescaling they differ by 0.050 dex, 46% of the observed scatter - so the barrier is finite: it is removed by measuring the interpolation shape, needing of order 5x the effective sample.

Fixing the kernel eliminates the systematic and yields a definite verdict, tabulated for five shapes: four of five favour a0 = (1/2) c sqrt(G rho_Lambda) at up to 2.69 sigma, the exponential kernel disfavours it at 0.66 sigma, and none reaches 3 sigma. The two dominant obstacles - the kernel choice (30.6%) and which cosmological density the horizon term tracks (20.9%) - both exceed the 7.87% being measured, so the present barrier is theoretical rather than observational.

Nothing here derives a coefficient. The reference value kappa = 1/2 remains fitted, not derived. Prior art is conceded in section 1 before any claim is made: the circular de Sitter response is partial prior art (Hari K. and Kothawala, PRD 109, 104073, 2024; Bunney and Louko, arXiv:2406.17643); the only novelty claimed is the extraction of a MOND coefficient from an orbital detector response, which was searched for and not found.

All numerical claims are reproduced by the self-checking scripts included in this record; each exits non-zero on any failed internal check.

description:
Recent attempts to derive Modified Newtonian Dynamics (MOND) and its characteristic acceleration scale a0 rely on the interaction between accelerated matter and the cosmological horizon. A persistent conjecture is that the vacuum response in de Sitter spacetime modifies inertia at low accelerations. In this work, we formalize this conjecture using Kubo linear response theory.

We postulate that the modification to inertia is dictated by a causal memory kernel K(t), derived as the inverse Fourier transform of the retarded susceptibility of the de Sitter vacuum. By computing this susceptibility for a massive scalar field in the Bunch-Davies vacuum, we show exactly that the equilibrium de Sitter vacuum is thermodynamically passive (it satisfies the Kubo-Martin-Schwinger condition). Consequently, the spectral density is non-negative, and the resulting inertia correction is strictly positive. The linear response of the de Sitter vacuum therefore raises inertia, an "anti-MOND" effect.

We conclude that any derivation of MOND from vacuum dynamics strictly forbids the use of dynamical memory kernels (influence functionals). Instead, we demonstrate that Modified Inertia must be formulated as a Category-2 thermodynamic Equation of State (EOS). By defining inertia as the excess response above the de Sitter thermal floor, the EOS approach bypasses the passivity wall entirely, yielding a causal, ghost-free relation that reproduces the exact MOND phenomenology without requiring non-equilibrium physics.

All numerical claims are reproduced by the self-checking script included in this record, which evaluates the worldline Wightman function directly to extract the susceptibility and mass correction.

title: The completion: a relativistic field theory carrying a_0 = kappa c sqrt(G rho_Lambda)

description:
A plain-language orientation piece, written deliberately as an anti-overclaim. It states one idea, the forty-year literature it sits inside, what the idea buys, and what remains broken — including one problem the author cannot currently fix.

THE IDEA. MOND fits galaxy rotation curves with a single dial, an acceleration a_0 ≈ 1.2e-10 m/s^2, whose value has never been derived. Its numerical resemblance to the cosmological acceleration, a_0 ≈ cH_0 ≈ c sqrt(G rho_Lambda), has been noted since the 1980s and has remained a coincidence. Working inside the Aether Scalar Tensor theory of Skordis & Zlosnik (Phys. Rev. Lett. 127, 161302, 2021) — the first relativistic MOND-like theory to pass the cosmic microwave background, and emphatically their result, not the author's — this piece describes setting a_0^2(Q) = kappa^2 G (-K(Q)), identifying the MOND scale with the dark sector's own pressure rather than inserting it by hand.

WHAT FOLLOWS WITHOUT ADJUSTMENT. (1) a_0 ceases to be a free parameter and is fixed by the dark energy density, giving a_0 = kappa c sqrt(G rho_Lambda) = 9.4e-11 m/s^2, with the residual coefficient kappa MEASURED (0.551 +/- 0.043), explicitly NOT derived — four candidate values lie within 2 sigma and the data do not select among them. (2) a_0 is forced to evolve, and it comes out near zero in the early universe and maximal today: 0.6% of its present value at recombination. MOND is therefore switched OFF when the CMB is imprinted, so passing the test that killed the previous generation of these theories becomes a consequence rather than a struggle.

PRIOR ART, STATED PLAINLY. The general move — letting a_0 depend on the dark-sector field so that a_0 evolves — is NOT new. Bekenstein & Sagi (arXiv:0802.1526, 2008) compute exactly this in TeVeS, finding a_0 varying as the exponential of the scalar field; Famaey & McGaugh's Living Review (2012) treats it as established background. What appears specific here is narrower: the identification with the pressure itself rather than with an exponential of the field (so no new function is introduced), the OPPOSITE sign of evolution (rising to a maximum today rather than decreasing), and the setting being AeST rather than TeVeS. The author states explicitly that this is a known idea implemented in a particular way, not a new idea, and that a full priority search has not been completed.

WHAT WORKS: c_T = 1 exactly; a no-ghost theorem; gamma_PPN = 1; a CMB fit computed with CLASS; SPARC rotation curves at 0.108 dex; the baryonic Tully-Fisher relation as a theorem rather than a fit; solar-system dynamics; weak lensing from 40 kpc to 2.2 Mpc.

WHAT DOES NOT WORK, AND IS NOT HIDDEN: galaxy clusters fall short by roughly a factor of two — MOND's forty-year-old open problem, unsolved by TeVeS and by AeST as published. This piece additionally reports why the author's own equation cannot patch it: the available amplitude reduces to the ratio of local dark-sector charge density to dark energy density, and even were that charge the entire dark matter content of the universe the term remains 100 to 1000 times too small. Two further open items are listed rather than omitted: kappa is measured and not derived, and the pressureless component the CMB requires is captured by galaxies and should collapse, with an endpoint in black holes that are not observed.

Every technical claim is backed by a runnable committed script in the accompanying repository, and withdrawn claims — several, including two of the author's own during the week of writing — are recorded there rather than quietly removed.
title: What I Found, In Context: The MOND Acceleration Scale as Dark-Sector Pressure, Its Prior Art, and What Remains Broken

description:
In relativistic completions of Milgrom's modified dynamics the acceleration scale a_0 is inserted as a constant of the theory and fitted to galaxy data. This paper observes that in the Aether Scalar Tensor theory (AeST) of Skordis & Zlosnik (Phys. Rev. Lett. 127, 161302, 2021) — currently the only MOND-like relativistic theory reproducing the cosmic microwave background — the dark sector already supplies a pressure, and that identifying A(Q) = a_0^2(Q) = kappa^2 G [-K(Q)] removes a_0 as an independent constant.

TWO CONSEQUENCES FOLLOW WITHOUT FURTHER ADJUSTMENT. (1) a_0 is fixed by the dark-energy density, a_0 = kappa c sqrt(G rho_Lambda) = 9.3619e-11 m/s^2 for kappa = 1/2. The paper states in its abstract that kappa is measured (0.551 +/- 0.043) and not derived — four candidate values lie within 2 sigma — and shows that the apparent depth of that question is illusory: because the pi cancels between sqrt(8pi/3) and Z, 'kappa = 1/2' is identically 'Z is twice the Friedmann factor', so the entire open content is one factor of two. (2) Independently of kappa, the dark-sector pressure evolves, forcing a_0^2(z)/a_0^2(0) = sqrt(1+nu_0^2) / sqrt(1+nu_0^2 (1+z)^6), which rises monotonically to a maximum today and gives a_0(z=1090)/a_0(0) = 6.0e-3. MOND is therefore ABSENT when the CMB is imprinted, making the parent theory's CMB pass structural rather than fitted.

PRIOR ART IS NAMED IN THE ABSTRACT. That a_0 may depend on the cosmological scalar-field value and hence evolve is NOT new: Bekenstein & Sagi (arXiv:0802.1526, 2008) computed it for TeVeS and obtained a_0 decreasing with time, and Famaey & McGaugh's Living Review treats the general statement as established. What is specific here is the identification with the pressure rather than an exponential of the field (so no new function is introduced), the OPPOSITE sign of evolution, and the AeST setting. No priority claim is made beyond that, and the paper states that no exhaustive literature search was performed.

WHAT IT PASSES: c_T = 1 exactly (GW170817); the parent no-ghost condition, which transfers because the two-field longitudinal conditions reduce to the two standard AQUAL conditions; gamma_PPN = 1; a CLASS CMB fit at Delta chi^2 = 1.34 over 4998 multipoles; SPARC rotation curves at 0.108 dex; the baryonic Tully-Fisher relation as a THEOREM rather than a fit; weak lensing from 40 kpc to 2.2 Mpc at chi^2/dof = 2.03 canonical / 0.94 alt; and the solar system.

WHAT IT DOES NOT PASS, AND A NO-GO FOR REPAIRING IT. Galaxy clusters remain short by a factor 2.08 at R500 (1.92 alt), rising to 4.21 inside 0.1 R500, on the twelve X-COP clusters. The paper then proves this construction CANNOT supply the deficit: the induced correction is Delta mu = -(rho_charge / rho_Lambda c^2) Phi T(y), in which nu_0, Lambda_D, Q_0, M and kappa ALL CANCEL, so the amplitude is a pure charge-abundance ratio. It supplies at most ~1e-9 against the ~0.5 required, and even setting the dark sector's conserved charge to the ENTIRE dark matter content of the universe leaves it short by 1e2-1e3. Two further open problems are listed rather than deferred: the pressureless excitation the CMB requires has no evident mechanism halting its collapse in galaxies, and kappa remains measured.

THREE FALSIFIABLE PREDICTIONS: no a_0 evolution below z~5 (any robust detection falsifies the law); rotation-velocity deficits of 0.34%, 7.8% and 18.9% at z = 10, 20, 30 via v(z)/v(0) = [a_0(z)/a_0(0)]^(1/4), detectable near z = 17; and a Gaia DR4 wide-binary velocity-boost ratio gamma_v = 1.2139 canonical / 1.2592 alt, the two footings separated by 2.68 sigma, registered before the data.

RevTeX 4.2 source and PDF. Every numerical claim is reproducible from committed scripts in the accompanying public repository.
title: The MOND acceleration scale as dark-sector pressure: a derived a0(z) that switches MOND off at recombination

description: The infinite monkey theorem is true and useless: a million monkeys typing 2 keystrokes per second on a 27-key keyboard need an expected 10^186063 years to produce Hamlet, because blind sampling has neither a prior nor a verifier. Interposing a large language model between the monkeys and the page collapses the expected wait to 2,400 years for the prompt 'write hamlet' and to about three minutes for 'hamlet' -- a compression of roughly 10^186060 in expected time -- because training has already absorbed the target's improbability into the weights, leaving the monkeys to find only its ADDRESS. We work the arithmetic exactly (every number in this note is reproduced by a committed script, monkey_compression_check.py, published alongside), derive the informational floor on prompt length (the address cannot be shorter than the bits of the target NOT already in the model; prompt length is a measurement of how much of a target's description already resides in the machine, and 'fame' is exactly the shortness of an object's address), and then make the serious point the joke carries: the same two ingredients that rescue the monkeys -- a prior that proposes only well-formed candidates, and a verifier that scores each one against data -- convert blind exploration into feasible generate-and-test search, the blind-variation-plus-selective-retention algorithm of Campbell and Simon with the language model playing chemistry and the data playing selection. This is a legitimate discovery methodology with one non-negotiable caveat, stated at full weight: SEARCH-UNTIL-FIT GUARANTEES A FIT, so the fit that terminates a search is a selection event and never evidence; evidence is what the surviving candidate does on data it was never searched against, and the supporting discipline is pre-registration with frozen thresholds, committed runnable verification scripts for every load-bearing claim, and a public ledger of kills and retractions alongside survivors. A short case study describes the author's own use of the loop (exploratory LLM prompting filtered by scripted confrontation with public galaxy kinematics), cited strictly for its methodology ledger; this note takes no position on the correctness of any hypothesis so found. The limits of the analogy (non-uniform elicitation, copying-fidelity, verifier quality as the binding constraint, and the prior-as-cage regression toward the known) are stated. Conclusion: proposal has become nearly free; confirmation has not; that asymmetry is now the entire game.
title: Monkeys, Hamlet, and the Price of a Prompt: Language Models as Search-Space Compressors in Generate-and-Test Discovery

description: The Aether-Scalar-Tensor theory (AeST; Skordis and Zlosnik 2021, PRL 127 161302) reproduces the Planck CMB power spectrum and the galaxy-scale radial acceleration relation, but leaves the scalar background rate Q0 = phi-bar-dot free -- its authors state explicitly that the dark-sector density is 'not (classically) predicted', and their three published fits span four orders of magnitude in Q0 (1e-4, 1e-1, 1 Mpc^-1). We show that a framework built on AeST with three additional commitments -- the dark-sector shift charge carrying the FULL dark-matter abundance (rho = Q0 n), the selection beta = 1, and w = -1 exactly -- collapses that freedom to a ONE-PARAMETER FAMILY, because the resulting relation Q0 = sqrt(Lambda) R_dm/(nu0 mu) is one equation in two unknowns. Galaxy-scale phenomenology then fixes the remaining coordinate: the framework's own kinematic identity slaves the condensate flow speed to the scalar gradient, and the same gradient must supply the static MOND force at radial-acceleration-relation radii. The result is Q0 = 3.4e-3 to 1.5e-2 Mpc^-1, equivalently K''(Q0) = 1e2 to 1e3, a region strictly interior to AeST's published fits. As an independent corroboration using no CMB information, expressing the result in the natural variable mu = sqrt(K''(Q0)) places BOTH of AeST's MOND-compatible published parameter sets inside the pinned band (mu = 122 and 195, band 33-1295) while the Higgs-type fit -- which Skordis and Zlosnik themselves call 'incompatible with a MOND limit' -- falls outside (mu = 41231). We are explicit about the limits: the pin is an order-of-magnitude CLASS statement rather than an equality (the two profiles equated have different radial shapes and the implied Q0 drifts by a factor 2.1-2.7 across 3.7-60 kpc); the value carries a CANDIDATE grade resting on one adversarially-refereed lane, though the identification of the framework's Q0 with AeST's own is derivation-grade and verified on five legs (units, cosmic time coordinate, background normalisation, kinetic normalisation, and the quasi-static relation) against the published source; K2 is pinned only to about three decades because the nu0 window propagates quadratically; lambda_s remains free; and kappa = 1/2 remains MEASURED (0.551 +/- 0.043), not derived. Most importantly, the result does NOT price the theory's nonlinear sector at recombination and cannot: AeST's authors note that a0 'does not appear in the linear cosmological regime but will play a role once nonlinear terms from F(Y,Q) kick in', which is precisely the regime at issue, so a Boltzmann computation carrying both the aether sector and the nonlinear branch at this framework's own kinetic function remains owed and is stated here as the sharpest open liability. The claim is narrow and checkable: IF one commits to the shift charge carrying the full dark-matter abundance with w = -1 exact, THEN galaxy-scale phenomenology alone selects a Q0 region interior to the published CMB fits, and specifically the region occupied by the MOND-compatible ones -- falsifiable by any CMB fit demanding Q0 outside 1e-3 to 1e-1 Mpc^-1. All quantitative claims are reproduced by committed scripts at https://github.com/carlzimmerman/zimmerman-formula, including the adversarial lane's own trial script and the standing retraction record. V2 NOTE (same day): section 5 is completed with the local-a0 analysis raised by the author -- a0 in this framework is a LOCAL quantity (A(Q) depends on the local charge density) and the pin radii sit inside halos, but the pin is a0-FREE ALGEBRAICALLY: Q0 = (g_tot - g_N)/(c v), in which a0 cancels identically, so the band is unchanged. The residual dependence is sub-linear and partly self-opposing; the band low end is soft by about 1.4x under the alternative steady-state-continuity reading of the local charge density, both inside the quoted envelope; and the same effect is what fixes the framework own nu0 ceiling, making it a priced rather than unpriced effect. Adjudicated in nbody_2026/stage59_local_a0_verdict_2026.py.
title: Pinning AeST's Free Background Parameter: Q0 = 2.4e-3 - 1.5e-2 Mpc^-1 from Galaxy-Scale Phenomenology

(1) Because the framework's a0 is a local quantity set by the dark sector's pressure at the local shift-charge density, the now-settled steady-state-continuity reading of the solar-circle charge flow makes the registered velocity-boost target a CONDITIONAL charge meter: at the charge floor the target moves by less than the frozen band's own width at every corner of the solar-overdensity bracket and both footings; at the ceiling the move is corner-split (-0.004 sparse to -0.093/-0.109 dense) -- DR4 measures the charge only if the solar-circle overdensity sits toward the dense corner, and settling that overdensity is the named prerequisite.
