description: Of everything a star owns, only its comet cloud extends into the regime where the acceleration scale a0 = kappa c sqrt(G rho_Lambda) = 9.36e-11 m/s^2 becomes dynamically relevant (r_M ~ 8,000 AU for the Sun). Three results, priced in both directions. (1) At solar-neighbourhood external fields the external-field effect removes almost the entire deep-MOND zone: an Oort cloud is Newtonian inside ~r_M and anisotropic quasi-Newtonian beyond, governed by the same committed response tensor (1.4732 parallel / 1.2598 perpendicular) as the hash-frozen Gaia DR4 wide-binary registration. A uniform gravity boost nearly self-cancels in comet-injection physics (the energy spike shifts only as G_eff^(1/7)); the surviving signal is directional: ~7% modulation of the spike position and ~17% of the injection rate with aphelion direction. (2) The exo-Oort version of this test -- KIC 8462852 (Tabby's Star) read through its dips -- is dead by 6.7 orders of magnitude: the dip-to-gravity inference chain leaks ~9e5x of model slack against a ~0.17 signal, priced arrow by arrow. (3) In the full relativistic completion the extra structure is silent at cloud scales (mass-term oscillation radius >= 23 kpc at the pinned Q0 band; a0-bump >= 280 kpc; a0(z) flat to 5e-7), but the pressure promotion makes a0 local, so the comet anisotropy becomes charge-dependent (16.7% at the nu0 floor, 12.1% at the ceiling) and CO-VARIES with the DR4 wide-binary gamma: one dimensionless charge moves both observables together. Constant-a0 MOND predicts a fixed 17% with no partner observable; the correlated pair is the framework-specific signature. This note prices a door; it claims no detection and freezes nothing. Every number is reproduced by a committed script.
title: The Oort Cloud as an External-Field-Effect Instrument: a Conditional Joint Signature with Gaia DR4

description:
V4 adds a new section: a candidate that satisfies R1 by construction. (i) The a0-line's AQUAL free function is derived in CLOSED FORM, f(z) = (1/2)sqrt(z)sqrt(1+4z) + (1/4)asinh(2 sqrt z) - sqrt(z) with z = (g_obs/a0)^2, and its deep-MOND limit is EXACTLY (2/3) z^(3/2) — the same 3/2 power and the same 2/3 coefficient AeST's own MOND term carries, with no free constant anywhere in the chain; the phenomenological relation and the host theory's MOND term agree at leading order because of what they are, not because they were matched. (ii) The beta=1 DBI kernel is shown analytic at its minimum with every odd coefficient vanishing (exponents 2,4,6,...) and a one-half power at its wall, so it supplies 3/2 at NEITHER location. (iii) A single-argument ansatz F(Y,Q) -> F(X) with X = (Q-Q_0) - Y/2m leaves the FRW background, w = -1 and the derived a0(z) law untouched by construction, and — using the theory's own quasi-static relation Q = (1-Psi)Q_0 — has X = -Psi Q_0 - Y/2m, so the free function's argument contains the Newtonian potential directly, satisfying R1 by construction. The mass m is fixed by the deep-MOND normalisation, hence by a0, and is not a new parameter. Recorded as OPEN, not as a result: a single ANALYTIC F cannot be quadratic at the origin and |X|^(3/2) at once, and the ansatz survives only because the two regimes sit on opposite sides of X = 0; the vector sector under the ansatz, the coupling to baryons against gamma_PPN = 1, and the pressure question are all unrun.

Aether-Scalar-Tensor gravity (AeST; Skordis & Złośnik 2021, Phys. Rev. Lett. 127, 161302) is the only relativistic MOND-class theory that reproduces the CMB power spectrum, and it contains a single free function F(Y,Q) that its authors leave unspecified. This paper shows that specifying it is obstructed, and extracts from the obstruction three necessary conditions on any relativistic completion of MOND phenomenology. Each condition is established by an explicit construction that satisfies the previous ones and fails the next, so the result is a filter on future theory-building rather than a single negative claim.

R1 — the free function must depend on the gradient of the TOTAL potential, not the scalar's own. With F(Y) the quasi-static reduction makes the scalar's own gradient the anomalous acceleration, and single-valuedness of F is equivalent to positivity of the longitudinal kinetic eigenvalue, which forces U(y) strictly increasing, which forces saturation U -> s, which produces a CONSTANT sunward anomaly s*a0 at every planetary distance. Perihelion precession then requires s <= 1.27e-5 (canonical footing) or 1.05e-5 (alternative), while the radial acceleration relation requires s >= 0.4348 pointwise, or 0.157-0.294 on the most generous global fit: incompatible by a factor 1.2e4 to 3.4e4. Crucially, this is specific to AeST and NOT to AQUAL, where the free function eats the total gradient and stability requires only d(g_obs)/d(g_bar) > 0 — satisfied by the exponential interpolation at minimum 0.968. The same kernel is legal in one theory and fatal in the other, purely from which gradient the free function eats. No relief exists: the external-field effect, computed for this family by two independent routes rather than imported, contributes exactly 1.000000x; a density-dependent a0 makes matters worse and is unsatisfiable below a suppression factor 0.080; solving the non-spherical problem for a Miyamoto-Nagai disc widens the requirement by 1.07-1.10x; refitting stellar mass-to-light buys 1.34x.

R2 — the cosmological background must not coincide with the deep-MOND end of the interpolation. AeST already contains the object R1 demands. An identity, verified three times independently and requiring no computer algebra, shows that AeST's aether-scalar mixing term is equivalent to an explicit +(2-K_B) a^mu a_mu piece, so the theory's apparent c_4 = 0 is an artifact of variables. Replacing F(Y,Q) by F(Z,Q) with Z = J^mu J_mu, the squared aether acceleration, then satisfies R1 exactly: J^i = grad^i Psi with unit coefficient, the quasi-static reduction becomes AQUAL exactly, the exponential kernel becomes legal, Newton's constant stays finite, and the 1 AU anomaly falls to 1e-3458.7 m/s^2 — some 3445 orders below the Sereno-Jetzer bound, replacing an anomaly that sat 1279x above it. The gap of R1 is voided. But Z-bar = 0 IDENTICALLY on FRW, so the cosmological background IS the deep-MOND end; linear cosmology sees K_B -> K_B - F_Z(0), and any F that performs the MOND interpolation has F_Z(0) = K_B exactly, so the aether's electric kinetic coefficient vanishes and the perturbation equation degenerates. F(Y) is protected only because J_Y vanishes at zero argument — the exact inverse situation.

R3 — and neither condition may be purchased with a split between the cosmological and local gravitational constants. Rescaling the free function repairs R1 and R2 simultaneously, with a non-empty window 0 < s < 0.138 at K_B = 0.25, leaving the solar-system screening untouched. The price is that the free function's normalisation becomes the sole source of Newton's constant, forcing Gtilde/G_N <= 0.121 (K_B = 0.25) or 0.048 (K_B = 0.10) against AeST's own 0.875 — an 8.3x to 20.7x split. It cannot be paid. Big-bang nucleosynthesis gives Y_p = 0.086 against an observed 0.2449 +/- 0.0040, a 42-sigma exclusion, with a closure-free backstop assuming no nucleosynthesis model at all still giving Y_p <= 0.176 at 17 sigma. The CMB result is an inconsistency rather than a tension: the gravitational sector's radiation density comes out at 0.2046 of the thermal photon density — below the gravitating density of the photons alone, whose value FIRAS fixes with no gravity anywhere in the chain — equivalent to N_eff = -3.503, missing the hard floor by 4.9x to 12.2x.

Stated against interest: gravitational waves do NOT pay this price, and the paper says so at equal volume. The tensor sector is exactly Einstein-Hilbert — on FRW plus a TT mode, J^mu = 0, Z = 0, F_munu = 0 and Y = 0 all hold identically and to all orders in the perturbation, so the dark sector carries no anisotropic stress for any free function — giving c_T = 1 and alpha_M = 0 exactly. The standard-siren amplitude's sensitivity to the rescaling is exactly zero and GW170817 places no bound. Two liabilities the same derivation creates are recorded but explicitly NOT scored, because the sharpest of them self-refutes: a tensor-only orbital-decay ledger giving an 8x deficit against B1913+16 would also exclude UNMODIFIED AeST at 77 sigma, so the ledger is incomplete rather than the theory dead.

Testable predictions. (P1) alpha_M = 0 and c_T = 1 exactly, for any free function, any rescaling, any K_B and both a0 footings — so this entire class is indistinguishable from general relativity in gravitational-wave propagation, and a confirmed alpha_M != 0 from LISA or Einstein Telescope falsifies all of it in one measurement, absorbable by no choice of free function. (P2) Any repair to the flux ledger must be period-INDEPENDENT, supplying the same fraction at every orbital period, because the decay ratio is measured at 0.16% in a 7.75 h orbit and 1.3e-4 in a 2.45 h one while a dipole enters at relative order (c/v)^2; the repair must renormalise the quadrupole coefficient itself. (P3) The F(Y) class predicts a constant sunward anomaly with a fixed planet ordering, already excluded. (P4) The F(Z) class predicts no solar-system deviation at any measurable level, ever.

Explicitly not claimed: that the three requirements are SUFFICIENT — they are necessary conditions extracted from three failures, and a completion satisfying all three is not thereby viable; that kappa = 1/2 is derived (it is FITTED, measured 0.529 +/- 0.034 from three determinations, with the distance-free one carrying an unpriced ~7% systematic); or that dark matter is absent (the full dark-matter density is retained here and the claim is "no dark-matter PARTICLE"). Whether the dark sector's dust remains bound inside galaxies is unresolved and untouched by any of this, being a Q-sector problem while all three constructions modify the Y-sector.

Unaffected, being independent of which completion carries them: the acceleration-scale normalisation a0 = kappa c sqrt(G rho_Lambda) = 9.3619e-11 m/s^2, the radial acceleration relation at 0.108 dex on 175 SPARC galaxies, weak lensing from 40 kpc to 2.2 Mpc with no dark component, the baryonic Tully-Fisher relation, and a hash-frozen wide-binary prediction decided by Gaia DR4.

Every quantitative claim is reproduced by a committed, self-checking script at https://github.com/carlzimmerman/zimmerman-formula; each prints numbered checks and exits non-zero on failure. Withdrawn claims are recorded, dated, in RETRACTIONS.md — including one in this paper's own drafting, where a gravitational-wave exclusion was written from an unverified number and corrected against the committed script before filing.

The contribution is the three requirements, the identity of section 3, and the constructions that establish them — NOT the underlying theory, which is Skordis and Złośnik's.
title: Three Requirements on a Relativistic Home for MOND Phenomenology

description:
The first construction in this programme with no computed kill against it — stated exactly, and not oversold: "no computed kill" is not "proven viable," and the two computations that decide it are named.

(i) A locality theorem. The Sun sits at 0.67-0.74 of its own galaxy's MOND radius, so the solar system and the MOND regime are the SAME environment. Between 1 AU and r_M the local gravitational field differs by 6.3e7, while the total potential differs by 1.5x, the dark-sector density by 2.2x, and the velocity dispersion not at all. Any mechanism suppressing the MOND force in the solar system must be keyed to a quantity differing by the required 1.2e4-3.4e4: ONLY THE LOCAL FIELD QUALIFIES. This kills environmental phase-boundary screening outright (the solar system and the outer galaxy are on the same side of any density/temperature/dispersion/potential boundary), closed this programme's own single-argument ansatz (squeezed by 4.3e3-5.7e3x, with the free mass scale cancelling from the ratio), and explains why requirement R1 of the predecessor paper (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22004372) demands the gradient: the requirement is forced by the Sun's position inside its own galaxy, not by formalism. Three prior deaths, one cause.

(ii) The scale identity is host-independent. The promotion a0^2 = kappa^2 G(-K(Q)) — the MOND scale IS the dark sector's pressure — and its derived evolution a0(a)/a0(0) = (1+sigma^2)^(-1/4) require only a shift-symmetric clock field on FRW. Both are re-derived by computer algebra with no reference to any aether or vector sector. Everything banked from that law — a0(rec)/a0(0) = 0.0060 (MOND off at recombination), the environmental bound nu0 <= 2.36e-6, the locality of a0 — carries over verbatim to any host supplying a clock field. They were K(Q) results, not AeST results.

(iii) The construction: bimetric MOND + the beta=1 DBI khronon + the promotion. BIMOND (Milgrom, PRD 80, 123536) has two metrics, matter coupled to one alone, the interaction built from the difference of connections — a tensor, with NO unit-timelike vector anywhere. Its favoured-class nonrelativistic limit is QUMOND, whose free function eats the LOCAL TOTAL FIELD: R1 and the locality theorem satisfied by construction. The legality condition d g_obs/d g_bar > 0 is met by the exponential interpolation everywhere (minimum 0.949 over 18 decades) even though that kernel's anomaly is non-monotone (peak 0.6476 at y = 2.540) — the exact shape that is FATAL in AeST is legal here, so the saturation trap's hypothesis is not met and the 1 AU anomaly is 1e-3458.7 m/s^2 (1e-3151.3 alt): the 1.2e4-3.4e4 ephemeris/RAR gap does not exist in this host. R2's vector-ghost mechanism has no counterpart (no vector, nothing for the Newtonian limit to poison); no Gtilde/G_N split is forced (R3); gamma_PPN = 1 is the literature's standing statement for the favoured class. The khronon (Q algebraic in d phi) supplies w = -1 exactly, dust excitations, and the conserved shift charge carrying the full dark abundance, unchanged.

Owed, stated plainly: (theory) a nonlinear Boulware-Deser ghost analysis — BIMOND's connection-difference interaction is NOT of Hassan-Rosen form, so the known exemption does not automatically apply, and BIMOND must not be quoted as ghost-free; (data) a Boltzmann computation, since the previous host's 0.01-sigma CMB pass does not transfer even though the dust component is identical. Also unchanged: the dust-binding problem and clusters. kappa = 1/2 is FITTED (0.529 +/- 0.034), never derived. There is no dark-matter PARTICLE here; the dark abundance is a field's conserved charge, present in full.

Every number is reproduced by committed self-checking scripts (superfluid_2026/sf01-sf07) at https://github.com/carlzimmerman/zimmerman-formula. Errors made and withdrawn during this programme are recorded, dated, with directions stated, in RETRACTIONS.md. Prior art on the a0-Lambda coincidence (Milgrom 1983/1999; Blanchet & Le Tiec 2009; Pikhitsa 2010; Klinkhamer & Kopp 2011) is credited: the coincidence is old; the identity and its derived evolution are this programme's contribution.
title: A Host for the Dark-Energy-Anchored Acceleration Scale: Bimetric MOND with a DBI Khronon

description:
A bimetric completion of MOND phenomenology carrying the acceleration-scale identity a0^2 = kappa^2 G(-K(Q)) -- the MOND scale as the dark sector's pressure -- pushed through every consistency gate the programme's published filter can pose. Every gate faced, passed; closure NOT claimed, and the two remaining items are named, one adverse-leaning.

THE CONSTRUCTION: two Einstein-Hilbert sectors; a shift-symmetric khronon whose beta=1 DBI kernel supplies dark energy (w = -1 exactly), a cold dust component carrying the full dark abundance as a conserved charge, and a DERIVED a0(z); and an interaction built from the khronon-projected connection difference, entering as V = sqrt(h)[N F(X) + Nhat B(X)]. The foliation is a dynamical field, not a gauge choice; full diffeomorphism invariance is kept.

SIX RESULTS, each with a committed self-checking script: (1) after the Hassan-Rosen-type shift redefinition, the projected connection C_M = (Gamma3 - Gamma3hat) - Khat u is EXACTLY lapse-free, and the interaction's lapse Hessian vanishes identically -- all four entries, not a diagonal zero. (2) The quasi-static reduction of a bimetric theory is a two-potential Moebius map, not AQUAL; inverting it for the a0-line g_obs^2 = g_bar^2 + a0 g_bar gives the interaction slope in CLOSED FORM, alphahat F' = (1-R)/(R(1+r)-1) with R = (sqrt(1+4x^2)+1)/2x -- single-valued and monotone, so the legality condition that excludes this same phenomenology in AeST is satisfied here. Free content: one function fixed by the a0-line plus ONE number r = M_f^2/M_g^2. The interaction switches itself off in the Newtonian limit: solar-system screening from the required force law, not a kernel choice. (3) The sign that makes gravity stronger is DERIVED: calibrating the EH quadratic coefficient against the Newtonian limit (M^2 = 1/8piG recovered exactly) forces the MIXED contraction C^i_jk C^j_ik = -|grad psi|^2. No negative coupling by hand. (4) Both lapses appear linearly; the relative shift is determined algebraically; the degree-of-freedom count is 7 = 2 + 5, the ghost-free bimetric number, conditional on one bracket. (5) THE GHOST TEST: {F(X), B(X)} = 0 identically (two functions of the same phase-space scalar), collapsing {C, Chat} to two cross terms; on an explicit lattice representative with EVERY constraint imposed at EVERY site and both controls passing exactly, the on-shell bracket is NONZERO at a generic real point. First-classness is universal, so the ghost-propagating alternative is REFUTED on the representative: the pair is second class and the Boulware-Deser mode is removed there. (6) The exact ADM kinetic reduction is then derived (exact Legendre transform, round-trip verified, exact sqrt(h)R3), and THE VERDICT SURVIVES IT UNCHANGED.

V2 adds result (7), the artifact verification: the representative's full-rank multiplier matrix (naively, frozen lapses) is dispatched by its own control -- PURE GR, first class in the continuum, FAILS THE IDENTICAL TEST on the identical lattice (on-shell brackets of rank 2 at magnitudes within 4x of the interacting theory's), and both obstructions move under a boundary-stencil change alone. The frozen-lapse finding is therefore a LATTICE ARTIFACT, uninformative rather than adverse. The ghost verdict is untouched: it rests on the bracket being NONZERO, and that direction's control (interaction off => bracket exactly zero) passed artifact-free on the same lattice. NOT CLAIMED: closure. Remaining, one theorem-grade item: the continuum Dirac analysis. Also remaining on the physics fronts: a Boltzmann run, lensing Phi+Psi, clusters, and the dust-binding question.

OBSERVATIONAL SHAPE: the derived a0(z) predicts an essentially STATIC baryonic Tully-Fisher normalisation across 0 < z < 20 (velocity shifts 1e-9 to 1e-6 at z = 1-5), then a cliff (1% at z ~ 26, 10% at z ~ 48) -- a shape no constant-a0 or smoothly-evolving-a0 model has, and two-sided: any robust per-cent-level detection of a0 evolution below z ~ 5 would need nu0 three to four orders of magnitude above its independent ceilings and falsifies the law outright.

kappa = 1/2 is FITTED (0.529 +/- 0.034), never derived; both a0 footings (9.3619e-11 canonical, 1.1279e-10 alt) are carried throughout; the a0-Lambda COINCIDENCE is prior art (Milgrom 1999; Blanchet & Le Tiec 2009; Pikhitsa 2010; Klinkhamer & Kopp 2011) and the IDENTITY is this programme's contribution. There is no dark-matter PARTICLE here; the dark abundance is a field's conserved charge, present in full. Six errors made during this programme -- roughly half manufactured deficits, half manufactured wins -- are recorded, dated, with directions stated, in the repository's RETRACTIONS.md, together with the standing rules extracted from them. Underlying theories: Milgrom's BIMOND/QUMOND and the Hassan-Rosen constraint mechanism; previous host analysis: Skordis-Zlosnik's AeST.

description:
For a shift-symmetric scalar with Lagrangian K(Q), where Q is the charge variable conjugate to the shift symmetry, the identity K'' = n/(Q cs2) holds with n = K' the conserved charge density. Since n > 0 and Q > 0 on any physical branch, the no-ghost condition K'' > 0 is equivalent to cs2 > 0, and therefore constrains only the sign of the sound speed — never its magnitude, and never its scaling with charge density.

This refutes a natural and easily made assumption: that stability forces such a condensate's sound speed to redshift as cs2 ∝ a-3, driving it to dust. That behaviour is the special case of a simple interior zero of K'. We exhibit an explicit ghost-free counterexample, K'(Q) = n1[1 + (s/c1)ln(Q1/Q)]-1/s, whose sound speed rises as the charge dilutes: cs2 = c1(n/n1)-s ∝ a+3s. Here K' > 0 for all Q > 0, vanishing only at the domain boundary and only logarithmically (298 decades of charge buy 6 decades of K'). Verification: K'' > 0 at 400 sampled charges across 45 decades in n, none skipped, minimum 4.9×10-27; the closed-form sound speed reproduced to 2×10-52 at 60-digit precision; and the w = -1 fixed point survives, relocated to the boundary of the charge domain.

Consequence: warm shift-symmetric dark sectors are not excluded by stability. Any argument of the form “ghost-free, therefore cs2 ∝ a-3, therefore dust” fails at its second step, and closure must be argued observationally instead.

Stated scope. Removing an obstruction is not building a theory. In the application that motivated this work, the warm branch was constructed and then failed three independent gates under adversarial review (GW170817 tensor speed; cluster scales at the low end of the charge window; and the radial acceleration relation, degrading 0.108 to 0.113 dex via a coherent deep-MOND tilt), with a required-sound-speed window short by a factor of 1.28. That is reported here rather than omitted. A methodological note records that the refuted assumption survived unchallenged in the authors' own work and failed for a recognisable reason — a correct near-a-simple-zero expansion generalised beyond its regime of validity.

All load-bearing claims are backed by scripts that exit zero; the counterexample was independently rebuilt from its defining ODE without importing the closed form.

description:
A Covariant Aether-Scalar-Tensor Framework with an Exponential MOND Constitutive Response


We formulate a covariant modified-gravity construction in the aether-scalar-tensor (AeST) class

in which the galactic modified-Newtonian-dynamics (MOND) response is fixed to the exponential

interpolation function µ(y) = 1−e−y. The proposal is built from a Lorentzian metric gµν, a

unit-timelike vector field Aµ, a scalar field ϕ, and a Lagrange multiplier enforcing AµAµ =−1. The

scalar-gradient invariant is taken to be Y = (gµν + AµAν)∇µϕ∇νϕ, while Q= Aµ∇µϕ controls the

homogeneous cosmological sector. We choose the free function so that its derivative with respect to

Y is exactly 1−e−√Y/a0(Q). In the quasistatic weak-field regime this produces the nonlinear MOND

Poisson operator ∇·[µ(|∇ϕ|/a0)∇ϕ], and in lapse variables the corresponding constraint can be

written as Di[(1−e−y)c2Diln N] = 4πGρm with y = (c2/a0) Diln NDiln N. The construction

separates the degenerate Y = 0 MOND branch from the homogeneous cosmological dynamics rather

than excluding either sector. We distinguish results inherited from the established AeST framework

from claims that are specific to the present constitutive choice. In particular, the paper does not

claim a completed global stability proof for the exact model function; instead it gives the action,

field equations, limits, consistency conditions, and a concrete set of falsifiable closure tests required

for such a claim.

description:
Preprint. This deposit timestamps three structural results with their reproducibility scripts; it is not a journal publication and makes no viability claim for any MOND theory.

For the single-invariant khronon carrier L = a₀²F(A²/a₀²) on a hypersurface-orthogonal preferred foliation, the scalar velocity-Hessian kernel is Zij = F′δij + (2F″/a₀²)āiāj, det Z = F′²(F′+2sF″). A genuine constant-rank scalar-removing degeneracy forces F′ = F″ = 0, hence F = const: wherever MOND is active (μ<1), Z⊥ = 2(1−μ) > 0 and the khronon propagates. Adversarially verified on FLRW and Bianchi-I backgrounds (θ, σ are invariants orthogonal to A²); isolated zeros of the longitudinal eigenvalue are strong-coupling surfaces, not Dirac constraints. description:
Preprint. This deposit timestamps a structural result and its reproducibility scripts; it is not a journal publication and claims no viable MOND completion.

Relativistic completions of MOND face a tension between reproducing the modified force law, preserving lensing, and keeping the degree-of-freedom count minimal. We report a systematic closure attempt across seven local architectures and extract two results.

(1) A cost table. Exact MOND requires deforming the GR Hamiltonian constraint away from the point where Hojman–Kučař–Teitelboim uniqueness applies, and each relaxation carries a distinct MEASURED cost: deforming the constraint algebra gives γPPN = 0 and α3 ≠ 0; spatial nonlocality damages the tensor sector (cT = 0) or the solar-system quadrupole; altering the momentum dependence propagates a scalar; altering the matter metric misroutes the source. We do not claim a universal no-go — HKT identifies a structural OBSTRUCTION CLASS for local metric Hamiltonians meeting its hypotheses, matched per-architecture.

(2) The AeST-collapse theorem (main result). The natural escape — paying for one extra propagating DOF via a screened (k-mouflage/Vainshtein) scalar — does NOT give a cheaper theory. Such a model passes five gates cleanly (3 DOF; cT = 1; γPPN = 1; the exact interpolation μ(y) = 1 − e−y; BTFR/RAR) but fails two, both BLIND TO THE DOF COUNT: (i) a conformally coupled scalar cannot bend light, because null geodesics are conformally invariant — the model predicts galaxies that rotate like MOND and lens like bare baryons, excluded by the observed agreement of the lensing and dynamical radial-acceleration relations; and (ii) the Cassini external-field quadrupole and the wide-binary signal are governed by the same interpolation-transition sharpness at the same external field η ≈ 1.9, so any screening clearing the former flattens the latter (this obstructs the TESTED external-field-kernel mechanism; screening keyed on a different environmental invariant — density, curvature, scalar charge, Vainshtein radius — is not excluded) (committed 175-galaxy scan: μ5/μ10 clear the Cassini ceiling at 0.39/0.08 while predicting γv = 1.0040/1.0001). Repairing (i) requires a disformal matter coupling; in every construction tested, that in turn requires preferred timelike structure of the kind carried by TeVeS and AeST, and a lensing-sized disformal term additionally splits the photon/graviton cones against GW170817. We state this CONDITIONALLY: within the tested class of local metric/disformal constructions, restoring the lensing channel requires additional preferred-structure degrees of freedom of TeVeS/AeST type — i.e. lensing APPEARS to cost a vector, not a scalar. This is NOT claimed as a classification theorem; establishing it needs a systematic classification of admissible couplings and their constraint structures, which we identify as the decisive next calculation.

Corollary. In the surviving class a0 is not structural, which relocates the framework's falsifiable content to the measurement side: a0 = κc√(GρΛ) with a0(z) ∝ H(z) is untouched by all seven obstructions (each fails on the COMPLETION, not on the acceleration scale). Gaia DR4 then becomes a sharp discriminator rather than a confirmation channel: Cassini-safe kernels predict γv ≈ 1.000–1.004 against a pre-registered band of 1.16–1.23.

Not claimed: a universal no-go for relativistic MOND; that HKT alone implies all seven failures; any derivation of κ or Z (both FITTED throughout); any exclusion of AeST itself — the point is that the 2+1 route offers no cheaper alternative to it.

title: An Obstruction Map for Relativistic MOND: the Conformal Lensing Barrier and the Cost of Its Repair

description: Relativistic MOND completions leave a factor-~2 missing-mass residual in galaxy-cluster cores. In Aether-Scalar-Tensor (AeST) theory the static weak-field equation for the potential is a modified Helmholtz equation, div[M(x) grad Phi] + mu^2 Phi = 4 pi G rho_b (Durakovic & Skordis 2024), whose homogeneous solutions oscillate; the boundary constant, 'the oscillation phase', sets an effective core mass and has been treated as a free parameter. A companion paper (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.20779562) found the resulting potential-depth lever real and galaxy-safe but descriptive, and named a 3-D N-body phase-pinning calculation as the single un-closed branch; three earlier dynamical solves found no pin because a free Klein-Gordon mode at omega = mu c is undamped. We show, from the action, that the phase belongs to a different branch. With K(Q) = K_2 (Q - Q_0)^2 and the k-essence identities p = L, rho = Q L' - L, the AeST Q-sector dust obeys p_d = (2 pi G / mu^2) rho_d^2, a gamma = 2 (Lane-Emden n = 1) polytrope, with c_s^2 = 4 pi G rho_d / mu^2 = 2w, and in a static well, where Q = (1 - Psi) Q_0, c_s^2 = |Psi| c^2 and rho_d = -mu^2 Psi / (4 pi G), exactly the Durakovic-Skordis phantom. Hydrostatic equilibrium of this polytrope IS the Helmholtz equation, and the free constant is the polytrope's Bernoulli constant, i.e. its captured mass; the n = 1 radius pi/mu is mass-independent, which is the whole freedom. The Klein-Gordon equation the earlier solves integrated has a Yukawa static limit and is the gapped branch. Because sign(rho_d) = sign(c_s^2), any static branch carrying dust on a potential hill has a gradient instability growing at |c_s| k (4.4 e-folds per Hubble time already at k = mu for |Psi| = 1e-6), so every node-bearing branch is excluded; all ten branches of the matched cluster boundary-value problem carry one. The physical configuration is the unique positive polytrope with a free surface inside pi/mu, and a one-dimensional Lagrangian gamma = 2 hydrodynamic solve of dust falling into the growing MOND well of a 1e15 Msun cluster reaches it (force residual 1%, Mach 0.10 residual motions, core mass ratio 1.00 to the static solution) while a +-50% free-mode admixture in the initial conditions changes the core mass by <= 3%: the phase pins. With the captured mass set to the cosmic dust share inside R500, the core (< 420 kpc) receives 2.3-3.4e13 Msun, 23-33% of the 1e14 Msun residual across both a0 footings and both interpolating kernels, galaxy-safe by geometry (a Milky-Way share leaves 9e7 Msun inside 20 kpc). The same configuration gives eta(R500) = 2.57 on the framework's kernel, within 10% of the raw eRASS1 value 2.33 with zero tuning, but overshoots the weak-lensing-corrected 1.7 on every kernel while undershooting the core: only 3% of the captured dust sits inside 420 kpc, because the profile rho_d ~ C - Psi cannot be more concentrated than the potential. The shape, not the amount, is the binding limit. The lever scales as (mu R)^2 and exists only at AeST's phenomenological mu^-1 ~ 1 Mpc. Two statements of the companion paper are withdrawn: the dust is not pressureless inside wells, so the density-ordering veto does not apply, and no N-body run is needed to settle the phase. The cluster core gap remains at least 65% open. All results are reproduced by committed scripts; a0, kappa and the dust amplitude I_0 are inputs, never derived.

description: Purely metric nonlocal realizations of MOND (Deffayet, Esposito-Farese & Woodard 2011; Woodard 2014; Deffayet & Woodard 2026) carry the MOND force in a retarded nonlocal scalar X = Box_ret^{-1}(R_mn u^m u^n) through an algebraic function f(Z), Z = (4c^4/a0^2) (dX)^2, and are the one class that escapes the local no-go for a relativistic MOND completion with Phi = Psi lensing and alpha_3 = 0. No perturbation analysis of this kernel on a MOND background exists. We perform it. Around a uniform MOND field (Z_bar = 4 y^2, y = g/a0), in Newtonian gauge and plane symmetry, at leading order in a0 -> 0 at fixed y, the scalar sector of the in-in theory (auxiliaries eliminated by their retarded particular solutions) has the dispersion (e+3) w^4 - (2e-1) k^2 w^2 + e k^4 = 0 at y = 1 for the exponential law, with discriminant 1 - 16e < 0: complex frequencies, Im(w) = 0.39 c k. The instability is present for every y >= 0.5 tested (Im w / ck = 0.21, 0.39, 0.44, 0.36, 0.18, 0.05 at y = 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8), grows without bound in k (e-folding 1.3e3 yr at 1 kpc, 13 yr at 10 pc), is longitudinal only (the transverse sector is stable), is driven entirely by f''(Z) -- the mu' term without which there is no MOND -- and appears identically for Deffayet-Woodard's own f(Z) = Z/2 exp(-sqrt(Z)/3). description:
A theorem: if a relativistic theory of gravity (i) reduces to Milgrom's modified Newtonian dynamics in the static weak field, (ii) carries a single physical metric to which matter couples minimally, and (iii) propagates exactly two gravitational degrees of freedom, then it contains a distinguished timelike direction — a preferred frame. Adding the elliptic boundary-value posing that Milgrom's equation actually uses, Frobenius makes that direction hypersurface-orthogonal: a preferred foliation, non-dynamical, with an instantaneous constraint.

The proof is three steps, each with its own controls. (E) MOND's variable is not a local scalar of the metric: a uniform field leaves every curvature invariant exactly unchanged while y = |∇Φ|/a0 changes by 1488× at 1 pc from a star, and a constant deepening of the potential is an exact isometry, so no functional of the metric — local or nonlocal, at any order — can measure a depth. The lemma is proved against an adversarial control invariant that is exact on Schwarzschild to 3.6 × 10−15 and then breaks by 87% on a binary, 9× on a disc and 11× in a Plummer core, and is 0/0 in a uniform field; physically, local curvature at the Sun's radius is nearest-star dominated over 99% of the volume and misses the Galaxy by 1487×. (Q) A symmetric form annihilating all timelike directions is identically zero (rank-10 solve); for one distinguished direction the null space is nine-dimensional and is exactly the spatial projector, so MOND's squared gradient is a projector contraction. (T) The principal symbol of the required extra structure is hyperbolic (it propagates, N ≥ 3), degenerate (it needs the distinguished direction), or absent (local, so E applies; or matter-built, which fails in the vacuum where rotation curves are flat and lensing is measured); there is no fourth case for finite-order field equations.

That finite-order proviso is the locality hypothesis, and it is discharged against the known nonlocal class by a mechanism that never uses locality: with no preferred timelike vector there is exactly one transverse symmetric operator, so every covariant scalar linear in the metric perturbation is a function of the d'Alembertian acting on the linearised Ricci scalar — the inverse d'Alembertian included, so nonlocality buys nothing — and therefore, for any frame-free covariant addition, with any weight and any coupling, ∇2(Φ + Ψ) = 8πGρ exactly: the lensing potential is welded to the baryons, and the rotation-curve and lensing equations cannot be modified separately. Adjoining one unit timelike vector makes the count two and unlocks them. This reproduces Soussa and Woodard's frame-free nonlocal result ("far too little lensing") and an independent proof that null geodesics are conformally invariant.

The escape was nonetheless real, and that is recorded: the mode count of retarded-nonlocal gravity is 2, not 4 — the localised counting rule overcounts even general relativity, whose conformal mode carries a wrong-sign kinetic term — so the nonlocal challenger satisfies (i), (ii) and (iii) at once. The theorem survives because the only nonlocal theory reproducing both MOND and lensing carries a unit timelike vector built as a normalised gradient, hence hypersurface-orthogonal, whose own authors describe its consequence as preferred-frame effects. A seventeen-theory control table (general relativity, RAQUAL, phase-coupling gravity, TeVeS, Einstein-aether MOND, AeST, khronometric, Hořava, BIMOND, MOG, Horndeski/DHOST, dRGT, modified inertia, the Deser-Woodard nonlocal class, and this programme's own three constructions) contains no counterexample; the pattern is an exclusive OR — Lorentz invariance XOR two modes — reported as an empirical observation over an enumeration, not as a proof. Mode-counting controls return 2, 3, 3 and 5 for general relativity, general relativity + scalar, khronometric theory and Einstein-aether. A constructive companion result closes the complementary question on four independent counts: no foliation-independent scalar can replace the slice-built field.

Because a preferred frame is not invisible, the theorem's constraint on the space of theories is turned into quantitative predictions with falsifiers, separated throughout into what is forced on any member of the class and what merely illustrates it in this programme's own action. The class is measured by the preferred-frame post-Newtonian sector — |α1| < 10−4, |α2| < 4 × 10−7, |α3| < 4 × 10−20 — and no member can set all three to zero by a symmetry it does not have. The corollary's instantaneous constraint is priced: where it has been computed, α3 = −1 as posed and −3 after the slip repair, i.e. 2.5–7.5 × 1019 over the pulsar bound, so the class faces a dichotomy — pay α3, or let the frame propagate — and this programme's own action takes the second horn with α3 = 0 and four modes. Read forwards, the lensing lock is a positive prediction with a size: every frame-free MOND theory lenses from the baryons alone, and the measured shortfall is 6.6× at cluster R500 and 46× (1.66 dex) at the deepest galaxy-lensing point, both ratios free of a0 and identical on the two footings. The extra structure has a measurable speed: |cT/c − 1| ≲ 10−15, satisfied structurally when the two aether couplings cancel, while gravitational Cherenkov bounds only slow modes (1 − cs ≤ 2 × 10−15 through a T00 vertex, 1.4 × 10−9 through a conformal one) and is switched off entirely by superluminality. And one fresh, sharply falsifiable prediction is stated with its price: the only live mechanism for the cluster shear shape — available only to a theory with a foliation, since a spatial smoothing needs a slicing — predicts a lensing-versus-dynamical mass slip of 0.02–2.3% for galaxies inside clusters against essentially none for the same galaxies in the field, decidable at 0.1% precision and measured nowhere near it today; its length is fitted, and at its ceiling it halves rather than cures the 9σ failure it was built for. Each prediction is stated as an observation and a threshold, and every dimensional number is carried on both a0 footings.

What is NOT proved is stated explicitly. This is a statement about theories satisfying the three hypotheses and nothing more: it does not close MOND-like theories in general — three or more propagating modes, two metrics, or a non-minimal matter coupling are all untouched. The locality hypothesis is discharged against the known nonlocal class rather than in general, and the residual computation is named (a nonlocal curvature scalar, quadratic or higher, that separates the Newtonian from the lensing potential while remaining sensitive to the coherent coarse-grained field rather than to the nearest star). The strict conclusion is a frame; the upgrade to a foliation is an added hypothesis. Nothing here says whether nature is MONDian — hypothesis (i) is an assumption about a theory, not a claim about data, and no observation is used anywhere to test the theorem; the measured quantities in the predictions section run only in the other direction, saying how large an effect a member of the class would have to show and what would falsify it. Sharpening it means beating the relation's intrinsic scatter, which needs better mass-to-light ratios and distances rather than better theory. The clock no-go is written at constant U and the tau-dependent case is not computed. The photocount identification is an identification: nothing here shows the vacuum response IS such a count. description:
A theorem: if a relativistic theory of gravity (i) reduces to Milgrom's modified Newtonian dynamics in the static weak field, (ii) carries a single physical metric to which matter couples minimally, and (iii) propagates exactly two gravitational degrees of freedom, then it contains a distinguished timelike direction — a preferred frame. Adding the elliptic boundary-value posing that Milgrom's equation actually uses, Frobenius makes that direction hypersurface-orthogonal: a preferred foliation, non-dynamical, with an instantaneous constraint.

The proof is three steps, each with its own controls. (E) MOND's variable is not a local scalar of the metric: a uniform field leaves every curvature invariant exactly unchanged while y = |∇Φ|/a0 changes by 1488× at 1 pc from a star, and a constant deepening of the potential is an exact isometry, so no functional of the metric — local or nonlocal, at any order — can measure a depth. The lemma is proved against an adversarial control invariant that is exact on Schwarzschild to 3.6 × 10−15 and then breaks by 87% on a binary, 9× on a disc and 11× in a Plummer core, and is 0/0 in a uniform field; physically, local curvature at the Sun's radius is nearest-star dominated over 99% of the volume and misses the Galaxy by 1487×. (Q) A symmetric form annihilating all timelike directions is identically zero (rank-10 solve); for one distinguished direction the null space is nine-dimensional and is exactly the spatial projector, so MOND's squared gradient is a projector contraction. (T) The principal symbol of the required extra structure is hyperbolic (it propagates, N ≥ 3), degenerate (it needs the distinguished direction), or absent (local, so E applies; or matter-built, which fails in the vacuum where rotation curves are flat and lensing is measured); there is no fourth case for finite-order field equations.

That finite-order proviso is the locality hypothesis, and it is discharged against the known nonlocal class by a mechanism that never uses locality: with no preferred timelike vector there is exactly one transverse symmetric operator, so every covariant scalar linear in the metric perturbation is a function of the d'Alembertian acting on the linearised Ricci scalar — the inverse d'Alembertian included, so nonlocality buys nothing — and therefore, for any frame-free covariant addition, with any weight and any coupling, ∇2(Φ + Ψ) = 8πGρ exactly: the lensing potential is welded to the baryons, and the rotation-curve and lensing equations cannot be modified separately. Adjoining one unit timelike vector makes the count two and unlocks them. This reproduces Soussa and Woodard's frame-free nonlocal result ("far too little lensing") and an independent proof that null geodesics are conformally invariant.

The escape was nonetheless real, and that is recorded: the mode count of retarded-nonlocal gravity is 2, not 4 — the localised counting rule overcounts even general relativity, whose conformal mode carries a wrong-sign kinetic term — so the nonlocal challenger satisfies (i), (ii) and (iii) at once. The theorem survives because the only nonlocal theory reproducing both MOND and lensing carries a unit timelike vector built as a normalised gradient, hence hypersurface-orthogonal, whose own authors describe its consequence as preferred-frame effects. A seventeen-theory control table (general relativity, RAQUAL, phase-coupling gravity, TeVeS, Einstein-aether MOND, AeST, khronometric, Hořava, BIMOND, MOG, Horndeski/DHOST, dRGT, modified inertia, the Deser-Woodard nonlocal class, and this programme's own three constructions) contains no counterexample; the pattern is an exclusive OR — Lorentz invariance XOR two modes — reported as an empirical observation over an enumeration, not as a proof. Mode-counting controls return 2, 3, 3 and 5 for general relativity, general relativity + scalar, khronometric theory and Einstein-aether. A constructive companion result closes the complementary question on four independent counts: no foliation-independent scalar can replace the slice-built field.

Because a preferred frame is not invisible, the theorem's constraint on the space of theories is turned into quantitative predictions with falsifiers, separated throughout into what is forced on any member of the class and what merely illustrates it in this programme's own action. The class is measured by the preferred-frame post-Newtonian sector — |α1| < 10−4, |α2| < 4 × 10−7, |α3| < 4 × 10−20 — and no member can set all three to zero by a symmetry it does not have. The corollary's instantaneous constraint is priced: where it has been computed, α3 = −1 as posed and −3 after the slip repair, i.e. 2.5–7.5 × 1019 over the pulsar bound, so the class faces a dichotomy — pay α3, or let the frame propagate — and this programme's own action takes the second horn with α3 = 0 and four modes. Read forwards, the lensing lock is a positive prediction with a size: every frame-free MOND theory lenses from the baryons alone, and the measured shortfall is 6.6× at cluster R500 and 46× (1.66 dex) at the deepest galaxy-lensing point, both ratios free of a0 and identical on the two footings. The extra structure has a measurable speed: |cT/c − 1| ≲ 10−15, satisfied structurally when the two aether couplings cancel, while gravitational Cherenkov bounds only slow modes (1 − cs ≤ 2 × 10−15 through a T00 vertex, 1.4 × 10−9 through a conformal one) and is switched off entirely by superluminality. And one fresh, sharply falsifiable prediction is stated with its price: the only live mechanism for the cluster shear shape — available only to a theory with a foliation, since a spatial smoothing needs a slicing — predicts a lensing-versus-dynamical mass slip of 0.02–2.3% for galaxies inside clusters against essentially none for the same galaxies in the field, decidable at 0.1% precision and measured nowhere near it today; its length is fitted, and at its ceiling it halves rather than cures the 9σ failure it was built for. Each prediction is stated as an observation and a threshold, and every dimensional number is carried on both a0 footings.

What is NOT proved is stated explicitly. This is a statement about theories satisfying the three hypotheses and nothing more: it does not close MOND-like theories in general — three or more propagating modes, two metrics, or a non-minimal matter coupling are all untouched. The locality hypothesis is discharged against the known nonlocal class rather than in general, and the residual computation is named (a nonlocal curvature scalar, quadratic or higher, that separates the Newtonian from the lensing potential while remaining sensitive to the coherent coarse-grained field rather than to the nearest star). The strict conclusion is a frame; the upgrade to a foliation is an added hypothesis. Nothing here says whether nature is MONDian — hypothesis (i) is an assumption about a theory, not a claim about data, and no observation is used anywhere to test the theorem; the measured quantities in the predictions section run only in the other direction, saying how large an effect a member of the class would have to show and what would falsify it. Nothing here says whether a preferred-frame MOND theory is viable; the α3 price is re-derived for one chassis and the universal form of it remains a conjectured obstruction, not a theorem, while no post-Newtonian computation exists for the nonlocal class at all. Every number is produced by a committed script with checks that can fail (fable_independent_2026/L31_foliation_nogo.py, L39_nonlocal_modes.py, L27_foliation_scalar.py, and, for the predictions, L13_strong_coupling.py, L24_lensing_vs_dynamics.py, L19_cherenkov_applicability.py and L57_nonlocal_functional.py and their supporting lanes in the public repository). description:
We examine the operator content of three scalar certificate families and supply explicit spectral comparisons where the stated hypotheses permit them. For radial stellar pulsations, we derive a Newtonian work identity and a self-adjoint general-relativistic form, distinguish homologous trial values from fundamental eigenvalues, and recover a post-Newtonian structural benchmark. For a discrete Dirichlet Hardy-type form with constant confinement, we obtain the complete finite spectrum and the sharp box-uniform spectral floor; direct action variations identify an obstruction to a proposed physical coupling identification. For the SU(N) Hamiltonian lattice gauge model at fixed lattice spacing, a full-space single-plaquette comparison gives an explicit gap for all N at the stated coupling, and an application of Yarotsky's weak-interaction theorem gives a sufficiently strong-coupling window uniform in N and open-lattice volume, including the canonical infinite-volume physical GNS representation.

The paper separates analytic proofs, applications of established external theorems, Lean-certified scalar results, and finite numerical checks. It does not assert a stellar mass cutoff, physical selection of the coupling kappa=1/2, a numerical many-plaquette threshold, or a continuum Yang-Mills mass-gap solution. The supplementary archive includes proof notes, Lean sources, reproducible computation scripts, results, and provenance records. The manuscript is CC BY 4.0; repository software in the supplement retains its AGPL-3.0-or-later license.
title: From Scalar Certificates to Spectral Bounds: Radial Pulsations, Discrete Hardy Forms, and SU(N) Lattice Gauge Theory

description:

This note reports two mechanism tests run in September 2026. Each rests on a committed script with a mutation control, re-run for this note, and the completion's algebra is certified in Lean 4 (62 theorems, zero sorry).

(i) Postquantum classical gravity (Oppenheim and Russo 2024) predicts a0 proportional to sqrt(Lambda) from stochastic metric noise. Its published coefficient is kappa = 1.30-1.45, at least 11 sigma above the measured value. Its linear term gives a lensing radial-acceleration slope of 0, against the KiDS-1000 value of 0.537 +/- 0.026. Around the classical saddle the fluctuation action contains no matter, so any rectified density is uniform: the slope is -1/2 (39 sigma), and a density large enough to act in galaxies would be at least 4e4 times the cosmic dark matter. A phantom made of gravitational-wave energy lenses at 0.75 of its dynamics (10.6 sigma). Constraint-violating static noise must lens at least 3.8 percent more than it attracts, which is 1.6 sigma today and not excluded, and the averaging convention is an O(1) systematic.

(ii) In the programme's covariant candidate C-H the MOND sector carries no momentum of its own, so the baryons cannot generate a phantom: at linear order the non-baryonic density seen by the leaf curvature is frozen. (In the nonlinear treatment, as in Blanchet and Skordis 2024, such a phantom is conserved and carried by the aether's flow, so whether an existing phantom follows a moving source is not established for C-H; the note states this scope.) Adding the khronometric alpha- and lambda-terms, with a monotone phantom law, gives C-H/K. Its phantom forms and follows moving sources, and its modes are free of ghosts and tachyons at leading order. Its Solar-System metric is that of general relativity at first post-Newtonian order (gamma = beta = 1 derived), and it leaves the SPARC fit unchanged. A moving source's phantom is amplified by 1/(1 - v^2/c_s^2).

Cosmologically, C-H/K fails as built. With the cold fluid the CMB requires, sigma_8 = 18-27. On FRW it is low-energy Horava gravity, and Planck-era bounds exclude the lambda-window that tracking needs; a leaf-average repair is offered. A switch keyed to the leaf curvature restores linear growth. It needs shear completion to pass GW170817, and by Gauss's law it makes isolated galaxies weigh only their baryons beyond its edge. It also leaves the cosmic web Newtonian, and the field that web exerts on isolated lenses (0.015 a0) excludes the construction on KiDS-1000 isolated lensing: Delta chi^2 = +404/+415 even with a free two-halo term. The Lyman-alpha forest verdict is borderline on the flux observable.

The note closes with the specification any completion must now meet, the doors it leaves open (a kernel blind to the large-scale field; a khronon sector that is itself dust on FRW), and the corrections carried on the record. description:

At the parameters that passed cosmology, the cubic term dominates the static equation in galaxies (the kinetic-sector density exceeds the MOND phantom by 1e8-1e12 at 10 kpc), and MOND ends at 1-4 kpc. The repair is withdrawn.

The relativistic khronon theory of Blanchet and Skordis (JCAP 11 (2024) 040) is run, on its own equations, through the two gates that closed this programme's previous completion (PAPER32).

Moving source: passed. The phantom is a conserved fluid carried by the aether, and a galaxy moving uniformly with its phantom is an exact post-Newtonian solution. The costs: the phantom is assembled rather than generated, it follows velocity changes only inside r ~ 2GM_b/du^2, and the static halo is stable only for a monotone phantom law.

KiDS's field bound needs it below 0.22 Mpc, while MOND-like lensing to 1 Mpc needs it above ~10 Mpc. The khronon-as-dark-fluid aether is therefore closed by KiDS for every K.

The mass budget. With CDM-like accretion, a conserved phantom of a KiDS lens runs out at 0.13-0.67 Mpc, inside the clean 0.3 Mpc range for most lens masses.

What stands. A one-scale MOND function J = Lambda j(Y/Lambda) makes a0 = kappa c sqrt(G rho_Lambda) an identity of the action, with kappa = 2 sqrt(8 pi)/(3 beta); kappa is not derived. The design lesson is that the MOND function must not read the acceleration of the cosmological dark fluid. AI-assisted research programme; not peer reviewed; nothing is claimed closed.

Reciprocity. If each species couples linearly to the fields of a static Lagrangian, the species-response matrix is symmetric. A dark component the kernel cannot see therefore feels Newtonian gravity only; a dark component that feels the baryons' MOND field while its own field stays unboosted has no action (it breaks momentum balance by a factor nu ~ r/r_M).

A kernel-invisible dark component exists as a Lagrangian construction (a subtraction pair of auxiliary fields). It leaves the baryons' boost, tracking and modes unchanged and predicts a dark-sector equivalence-principle violation: at R500 in X-COP clusters the dark component feels 47% (37-53%) less acceleration than the gas.

Blindness to dark matter is not enough. A kernel that reads all baryons still feels the web's baryonic field, about 30 times what KiDS-1000 isolated lensing allows. The globular-cluster dispersions of 19 SLUGGS early types, which the law leaves +0.080 dex short (3.3 sigma), are fitted at +0.007 +- 0.017 dex (0.4 sigma).

Costs and limits. Added to the programme's 48-gate harness, the rule moves SPARC by 0.0009 dex and the cold budget by at most 0.007 of Omega. One massive S0 in SPARC disagrees by +0.14 dex. Satellites and the coefficient. The programme ties the MOND acceleration scale to the vacuum, a0 = kappa c sqrt(G rho_Lambda), with kappa = 1/2 fitted, not derived. Its distinctive high-redshift prediction is a flat a0(z) (distinctive against LambdaCDM and the H(z) rival; standard MOND shares it); the rival is a0 proportional to H(z) (about x2.2 at z~1.4, x8 at z~5); LambdaCDM has no a0 and enters only through an effective-a0 proxy. We collect the programme's committed high-redshift a0 lanes and state one result plainly: in every lane the limit that survives an unlimited sample is the absolute calibration of the baryon (gas and stellar) masses; at present sizes the KiDS split, the class-S sources of the compilation and the seven class-M galaxies are also limited by statistical power or by the Newtonian regime (CFG255, CFG227, CFG229).

The lever. Where the discs sit (per-point median g_bar/a0 = 1.1 to 4.4) a 0.05 dex error in the mass discrepancy is a factor 1.5 to 1.8 in a0; the implied a0 moves by -2.5 to -4.8 dex per dex of baryon mass (a post hoc finite-difference estimate at a +-0.03 dex step; -2.5 to -6.4 at +-0.01 dex). In the deep regime an amplitude test measures only the product of the calibration and a0. Lean theorems (ChainCert, 331 theorems) show that a0 remains identifiable in principle for the exact kernel, but the estimate is ill-conditioned: with the calibration free, and for local kernel slopes in [0, 1/2] with independent Gaussian errors, sigma(log a0) >= 3 sigma/sqrt(N); a log-uniform sample of 20 galaxies at 0.1 dex must reach g_bar/a0 of about 8 and include deep points to measure a0 to 0.1 dex.

The samples. No sample separates the laws: RC100 is gas-route-limited, CRISTAL is route-dependent, and the z = 2-5 compilation, the ALMA [CII] rotators and seven class-M galaxies are NOT POSSIBLE at pre-flight. The gas calibration at z~2.2 is a prescription bracket (~0.2-0.7 dex), and no public dynamics-independent anchor reaches 0.10 dex: the best route, an absorption-line alpha_[CI](Z) relation, does not reproduce its stated 0.2 dex scatter from our transcription of its Table 1 (0.64 dex about the quoted relation; how the authors define that scatter, and any erratum, were not checked; an apparent cyclic shift in four rows is a hypothesis not put to the authors). A within-survey lens-redshift split of the KiDS-1000 lensing RAR, which would cancel a common-mode calibration, is NOT POSSIBLE (power 0.14 against 9) and non-discriminating by its own control; even with unlimited statistics a stellar-mass drift delta would mimic an a0 drift by delta/2.

Bottom line. A decisive a0(z) test needs baryon errors and band at or below 0.10 dex. With the public data on hand the question is open; nothing here is a detection either way, and nothing here says the data favour the framework, the rival or LambdaCDM. The near-term test of the programme is a separate z = 0 one, which its current candidate law can only survive or fail: Gaia DR4 wide binaries (2 December 2026). description:
Version 1.0: the first deposited version (internal revision 1.2; not peer reviewed). Revision history: an undeposited first draft read the catalogue line widths as observed-frame and divided them by 1+z; the catalogue paper's own worked examples show they are rest-frame, which a frozen follow-up test confirmed, so the rest-frame reading is primary; a second review added the frozen single-dish reading to the flux-scale range, both distance conventions and two statistical-error estimates to every footing statement, and the selection term to the abstract. The observed-frame numbers are kept as a disclosed variant.

The programme ties MOND's acceleration scale to the vacuum, a0 = kappa c sqrt(G rho_Lambda), with kappa = 1/2 fitted, not derived; its footings are 9.3603e-11 (rho_Lambda) and 1.1312e-10 m s^-2 (rho_crit). We apply a width chain, frozen before any width was read, to the MeerKAT MIGHTEE-HI COSMOS catalogue: V comes from the rest-frame W50 and inclination, the baryons are 1.33 M_HI + M* at half the HI diameter, and a median-residual estimator with the exponential kernel returns a0. Forty-seven golden discs at 0.027 <= z <= 0.093 survive, all at g_bar/a0 <= 0.084, 37 gas-dominated.

Result. On the catalogue's flux scale and H0 = 70 distances a0 = 1.31e-10 m s^-2 (statistical +-0.034 or +-0.048 dex, by bootstrap or per-galaxy spread; recipe +-0.128 dex), kappa = 0.70 or 0.58: consistent with SPARC and the alternative footing, with the canonical footing 0.019 dex outside the recipe width. On the H0 = 67.4 distances of rho_Lambda (a0 = 1.21e-10) the canonical footing is inside it (0.111 dex away). Arecibo fluxes exceed the catalogue's for brighter, nearer galaxies; applied to our discs' gas they give 0.90-1.13e-10 (0.90 for the frozen pairs, 1.07 for a post hoc extrapolation), inside the recipe width of both footings. Line-width corrections lower a0 by up to 0.10 dex; kernels without the exponential's next-order term raise it by 0.06-0.07 dex; dropping the S/N cut, by 0.08 dex. A SPARC closure tests only the baryon recipe. The width frame rests on the catalogue paper's worked examples; independent data tests could not decide it, and all three lean weakly towards the observed frame.

What it can and cannot say. The result is not a footing discriminator and, with a lever of 0.009 dex, not an a0(z) test. The cold mass (Omega_c h^2 ~ 0.12) is still required; no dark-matter particle is added; no preference of the data for one reading over another is claimed.

The programme ties the MOND acceleration scale to the vacuum, a0 = kappa c sqrt(G rho_Lambda), with kappa = 1/2 fitted, never derived. Its best current effective law, candidate B, is the MOND kernel plus hierarchical ownership (only the outermost bound system carries the phantom) plus a cold component with the cosmic amount Omega_c h^2 ~ 0.12: the mass is still required, and no dark-matter particle is added. No committed action produces B. This note is a map of failed routes and a reading of what they suggest, not a result.

The gaps. Three gaps separate B from a mechanism: a legal owned switch (Gap 1), the cold fluid that is the law's dark density (Gap 2), and the a0-Lambda tie with its coefficient (Gap 3).

What Lean certifies. A Lean library of 331 theorems (standard axioms only) certifies, from stated premises, that the postulated ownership rule is not a function of the internal and external field at a point, that a continuous law with no external-field effect is linear, that among monomials a length proportional to M^(1/2) needs an acceleration scale, and that an AQUAL action gives the kernel in spherical symmetry; it certifies no empirical fact.

The routes. We tabulate 25 committed routes: 22 are scoped no-gos on their frozen classes, two owner-directed lanes find no mechanism (11D's hand-check, and CFG253's background calculation, which asks where the cold amount comes from; without it the count is 24), and one shows realisability only. None is a mechanism. Every route's criteria were written before its scripts; for 20 of the 25 they were committed first, and for five they were committed together with the scripts, as the lanes disclose.

A reading of the requirements. The failures suggest a specification. It is a reading of the scored classes, not a theorem: only the acceleration-scale item rests on a theorem (for monomials) and the cosmic amount on the inherited CMB gate; the rest rests on the failure of one to three scored classes per item. The reading asks for an early cold fluid present before structure forms (a dust created at turnaround supplies Omega h^2 = 0.1200 x 10^-1376.8 at z = 1100); ownership that remembers boundness (a causal latch keeps n = 0.791 at one free-fall time against the required 0.99); a distribution that carries the M^(1/2) scale itself (passive bound infall scales as M^(0.33-0.34), and relaxation at a vacuum-set rate reaches Gamma tau <= 0.79 against the ~4.1-4.2 needed); a target that is field-local in the Newtonian field but needs bound-domain labels; and no created rest mass.

Satellites and the coefficient. B's ultra-faint failure (3.5-3.9 sigma) does not move under the 2026 binary-corrected and DEIMOS dispersions, and Gate H leans toward the bound-core (LambdaCDM-comparator) reading at satellites by small margins (planted-sample power 0.28, carried entirely by the ultra-faints): a lean, not a detection. kappa = 1/2 is fitted (0.465 +- 0.076 from the baryonic Tully-Fisher relation), and Milgrom's cH0/2pi footing fits SPARC at least as well as either framework footing.

What decides. Gaia DR4 (2 December 2026) is a survival test of B against the merged (no-ownership) law: decisive against Arm A's nu_RAR kernel (floor 1.161, alt 1.192; the preregistration falsifies Arm A below 1.056), but only 2.3-3.7 sigma against the P2 kernel (merge 1.063-1.102 canonical, N = 30,000), and no separation from the derivation chain's ceiling; B, LambdaCDM and Newton all predict gamma-hat = 1.000, and 1.084 <= gamma-hat <= 1.23 falsifies B if the frozen stability requirements pass. For the flat a0(z) law against a0 proportional to H(z), the limit that survives an unlimited sample is the absolute baryon calibration; at present sizes several lanes are also limited by statistical power or by the Newtonian regime (PAPER38 version 1.2, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23085582).

Every number carried by an audit row is re-read from committed files by PAPER39_audit.py (201 of 201); the tex is checked at block level, not sentence level, and numbers quoted only in running text are not checked by the script. The menu of routes was written knowing the target, and the referees were not blind. AI-assisted research programme; not peer reviewed; nothing here is claimed closed.

description:
The programme's central relation ties the MOND acceleration scale to the vacuum, a0 = kappa c sqrt(G rho_Lambda), with kappa = 1/2 fitted, not derived. This note reports a principle that decides which systems the law acts on, the scorecard it earns, and the prediction it makes for Gaia DR4 before the data exist.

Hierarchical ownership. The law acts on a system's own baryons only if that system is the outermost bound system. An accreted satellite keeps the dark component it owned at infall; a system that formed embedded in a host (a tidal dwarf, a globular cluster, collision debris, a wide binary, the Solar System) is Newtonian. The rule adds no constant and removes one, the Solar-System screening length.

Scorecard. On the record's population gates it passes 9 of 14, against 6 for the same law with the host's external field. With the infall baryons its own logic calls for, the M31 satellites pass (1.2-1.6 sigma), and the combined target law passes 42 of 48 harness gates. It fails two: the Milky Way's ultra-faint satellites (3.5-3.8 sigma once refereed, first quoted at 7-8 sigma on statistical errors alone; the external-field reading fails them at 13 sigma) and the external-field signal of Chae et al. (4.1-4.3 sigma in their fits; 1.7-2.2 sigma refit under the framework's own law at the canonical scale).

Shape. A cold component in local virial equilibrium around a point mass reproduces the kernel nu = sqrt(1 + 1/y) exactly, with a0 as its charge per unit baryonic mass; SPARC disfavours that kernel's transition shape at about 2 sigma.

Dark sector. The dark sector's edge meets a 5.4 sigma tension between KiDS-1000 lensing and the cosmic cold budget. The same lensing machinery misfits standard LCDM halos by at least Delta chi^2 = 50, so the tension is not decidable there. The Local Group's zero-velocity radius conflicts with standard halos at least as strongly as with the framework.

Prediction. Wide binaries are exactly Newtonian: gamma_v = 1.000 on the pre-registered Gaia DR4 estimator, falsified at gamma_hat >= 1.084. The same law with the external field predicts 1.16-1.23 and is falsified by a Newtonian result. Gaia DR4 is scheduled for 2 December 2026. Every quoted number is re-derived from committed outputs by PAPER35_audit.py (98 of 98). AI-assisted research programme; not peer reviewed; nothing is claimed closed.

description:
Preprint (Author's Original Version): submitted to Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society; not peer reviewed. This is the version as submitted, posted under the publisher's self-archiving policy for the author's original version. If the paper is accepted, this record will be updated with the journal DOI.

The galactic acceleration scale a0 is close to c sqrt(G rho_Lambda), built from c, G and the density of the cosmological constant. We write a0 = kappa c sqrt(G rho_Lambda), measure kappa and ask what testing its evolution requires. On SPARC, with distances and rho_Lambda on one H0, three estimators give kappa = 0.45 +- 0.07, 0.58 +- 0.18 and 0.43 +- 0.08. The value 1/2 is consistent with all three, as are Milgrom's c H_Lambda / 2pi and c H0 / 2pi; on the critical density it lies 2.1-2.2 sigma from two, and a published joint inference puts it at 2.6 sigma. The coefficient is fitted, degenerate with H0 and set by the stellar mass-to-light zero point. A Lambda-anchored scale is constant; one tied to the critical density grows as H(z) (+0.58 dex at z = 2.5); LCDM haloes of low-acceleration discs give +0.22 dex. Existing samples decide nothing. With stellar-population masses plus scaling-relation gas, the baryons exceed the dynamics in 41 of 100 discs at 0.6 < z < 2.5 (half of those at z > 2), so this route measures the baryon calibration, not a0. The MUSE-DARK rise at z ~ 1 is not recovered with these masses, though which masses are biased is unknown; a lean towards a0 proportional to H(z) at z ~ 1.5 turns on unmeasured gas and pressure support. Inferring a0 amplifies errors unless g_bar < 0.3 a0. Expected odds of 20:1 need about eight lensed discs at z ~ 2.5 measured to 0.20 dex if the baryonic-mass calibration is exact, 20 or 34 if it is shared to 0.05 or 0.06 dex; no gas tracer yet provides that.

Every quantitative statement is produced by a public script whose checks can fail (paper_numbers.py and reproduce_all.sh in the linked repository, at the tag of the submitted version). Generative AI tools assisted with code, literature checks, table transcription and drafting (Anthropic's Claude, and models from OpenAI, DeepSeek, Zhipu AI, Alibaba, Google, Tencent, Moonshot AI and xAI); the author checked every result and takes sole responsibility for the content.

description: VERSION 3 IS A CORRECTION RELEASE. In an independent claim-by-claim audit, every sentence of v2 containing a number was traced to the file a script wrote. The headline result and every conclusion stand. Twelve statements carried wrong numbers, six overstated what the outputs show, and seven numbers had no saved output. The scripts behind them were re-run, their outputs are now saved, and all are corrected; Section 11 of the paper lists what changed. THE NULL (unchanged). Every dimensionless value constructible at depth <= 10 from the framework's two germs (the generation count 3 and the kernel germ sqrt(8pi/3), with a0 = cH_Lambda/Z, Z = sqrt(32pi/3)) was confronted with 19 measured Standard-Model targets: 174,890,804 raw candidates, 42,534,139 distinct values, 82,613 in-window hits, ZERO surviving the false-discovery gate. Depths 6-9 are clean nulls under the same engine, depths 3 and 5 under earlier forced-exhaustion engines, and depth 4 is structurally empty there (no dimensionless expression fits the depth budget). WHERE THE HITS LAND. Hit count tracks window width and nothing else: the six most precisely measured targets (relative half-widths 1.1e-10 to 1.9e-7) return zero hits; the PMNS angles (2.5e-2 to 4.0e-2) return 15,212 / 26,142 / 20,799. THE CEILING. Single-target matching becomes uninformative by ~D11-13. Our depth 10-18 sampling campaign (1,191 passes, 18,332 hits, all FDR-DEAD) was empty by construction. The published ceiling formula was wrong: B = 30 is the menu length, and the realized branching factor is 4.41. THE MAIN LESSON. The proposed multi-target bits rule priced an impossible object (one expression matching k targets). The real object is a skeleton reaching k targets via k recipes, so the look-elsewhere cost is paid k times. A label-permutation null is harsher still: chance alone reaches ~11 of 18 targets on one skeleton. A validated interlock search finds max k = 10 against a chance maximum of 11.0, p = 1.0. WITHDRAWN IN v2 AND STILL WITHDRAWN: a valid held-back validation set (both holdouts are exact algebraic functions of fitted targets) and 'forced' as a filter (on the enumerated path Gate B is a constructive tautology; hand-fed self-declared candidates can also clear it, which is unreachable from the enumerator). WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. No new statistics; nothing about depth 11+ or other vocabularies; the search neither supports nor damages the gravity framework whose germs it uses.

description:
Working note, version 2.2 (2026-10-10). AI-assisted research programme; not peer reviewed. Version 2.2 corrects the growth claim of versions 2.0 and 2.1: their numbers were measured on the particle field; on the gravitating field the rule fails at 512^3.

Correction (2026-10-10). Every growth number in v2.0/v2.1 was measured on the particle density. The rule moves cold fluid within each catchment and that mass gravitates, so the matter power spectrum (what weak lensing, cosmic shear and sigma_8 respond to) is that of the particles plus the settled source. Re-measured on that density from the same saved z = 0 states (lane CFG555): all twelve 256^3 runs pass (max|P-1| = 0.063-0.082, sigma_8 ratio 1.014-1.019), but all four 512^3 runs fail the 10% spectrum cut: canonical 1.0405 / 0.163 (the headline row), alternative 1.0459 / 0.193, a0 tracking dark energy 1.0429 / 0.167, and the second 512^3 realisation 1.0333 / 0.184. The mass-conservation control (no compensation) is 1.1730 / 0.505 on this density. The comparison rows (edge set by hand, edge from census retention) and the +15.3% / +19.3% / +17.4% 'law everywhere' numbers are also particle-field numbers and were not re-measured.

We study the law a0 = kappa c sqrt(G rho_Lambda) (kappa = 1/2, fitted) with the kernel nu_mono (equal to nu(y) = 1/(1 - exp(-sqrt y)) for y <~ 2.5, with a monotonic tail above; it differs only in the near-Newtonian regime, by <= 2.4% at y = 10-30) and a cold fluid of fixed cosmic amount. In particle-mesh simulations, letting the law act wherever matter has collapsed makes small-scale structure too clumpy: the excess in the particle power spectrum at k <= 1 h/Mpc is +15.3% / +19.3% on the two footings at 256^3 and +17.4% at 512^3, against an allowed 10%. We test one rule with no tuned radius. The law's extra (phantom) mass is the cold fluid itself, so a halo can build the phantom only until its own cold fluid is used up (for an undepleted halo at r_edge = r_M / ln[1/(1 - f_b)] = 5.85 r_M), and the cold fluid used is drawn from the same halo's turnaround sphere, so mass is conserved halo by halo. With this rule the excess in the particle (baryon-tracing) power spectrum is 2.7% at 256^3 and 3.3% at 512^3, with sigma_8 within 0.6% of a control run without the law (cold fluid evolved as ordinary cold matter, i.e. LCDM-equivalent growth): 15 of 15 runs pass on the particle density. In the gravitating matter density the excess is 6.3-8.2% at 256^3 but 16-19% at 512^3 (sigma_8 +3-5%), above the 10% limit, in every 512^3 run; 12 of 15 pass. Structure growth as seen by lensing is therefore not fixed by this rule, and the gap grows with resolution.

The rule adds no tuned radius or width; its framework inputs are kappa and the cosmic baryon fraction, and it inherits standard ingredients (LCDM initial spectrum, spherical-collapse turnaround density, halo finder, pass thresholds). The cold fluid is handled as bookkeeping, not as simulated particles; its settling is imposed, not derived from an action; and kappa, the cold fluid's amount and rho_Lambda remain undetermined. No dark-matter particle is identified. Every number is checked against committed outputs by PAPER45_audit.py (44/44). AI assistance: Anthropic's Claude and DeepSeek.
title: The Supply Edge: A Mass-Conserving Rule Without Tuned Radii Under a Vacuum-Tied MOND Law Keeps Particle Clustering Within 10%, but Not the Gravitating Matter Spectrum at 512^3 (Working Note)

The dated releases ahead are the ALMA cubes of 2026-11-06 (U4_27928) and 2026-11-28 (GS4_24110) and Gaia DR4 on 2026-12-02 (wide binaries; the Milky Way vertical force and outer curve, sealed in advance). description:
Version 1.1 (2026-10-13) corrects the action as written in v1.0: the completed-square term must be paired with the remainder potential W_rem = W_full - u^2/(8 pi G), not the full saturating potential (which double-counts the critical quadratic and, taken literally, gives nu -> 2). With W_rem the Euler-Lagrange equations give exactly g_N = g^2/(g + a0) (checked numerically: nu = 100.5 at g_N = 1e-4 a0). No result in the note changes; the selector calculations already used the residual form. Correction found by the programme's parallel reviewer.

Working note, version 1.0 (2026-10-13). AI-assisted research programme; not peer reviewed.

We work with the acceleration law a0 = kappa c sqrt(G rho_DE) (kappa = 1/2, fitted), equivalently a0 = 0.173 c H_inf, where H_inf is the asymptotic Hubble rate of a cosmological-constant universe. The law is written as the static limit of a single action for a polarization field P with a saturating vacuum term W'(u) = u/(1 - u/a0) (no new constant), giving g_N = g^2/(g + a0); it fits raw SPARC rotation curves (0.1009/0.0994 dex) and, with free-fall basins and a stiffness rule, passes wide-binary, cluster-satellite and star-node tests.

Reading the data first, we find cold energy plausibly comes in two kinds. (i) The field's bound charge has zero net mass and no inertia, so it cannot be the collisionless mass clusters, the Bullet Cluster, Local Group timing and the cosmic web require. (ii) Only a carrier with real rest mass meets the evidence; the viable carrier is a cold collisionless medium whose displacement is P. (iii) That coupling yields a conservative tether with the law as its unique static minimum and a capacity Sigma <= a0/(pi G) (214/258 Msun/pc^2). (iv) In raw SPARC data galaxies sit below the capacity (median ~0.3 of it), while the Bullet Cluster's cores hold 3.6-4.8 times it. Cold energy is therefore plausibly tethered (law-shaped, capped) in galaxies, with a free collisionless component pooling in massive cores, a candidate for the excess core mass measured in early-type galaxies, groups and 318 eRASS1 clusters. If the medium is a condensate, the data still allow its self-interaction (sigma/m <= 0.71 cm^2/g vs a required 0.11-0.82).

We list six framework-specific predictions, including a decisive one (the free central density in relaxed clusters), and the limitations: the carrier is particle-like; kappa is fitted and Omega_c/Omega_b measured; the capacity rests on stated conditions; hot vs condensed baryons is unresolved; massive early types still fail (Z ~3.7); the programme's full raw-KiDS shear test is pending; Bullet lensing masses are provisional. Nothing here closes the theory. AI assistance: Anthropic's Claude.
title: Two Kinds of Cold Energy: A Capacity-Limited Tethered Component and a Free Core Component Under a Vacuum-Tied MOND Law (Working Note)
