We test a gravity framework in which the acceleration scale is tied to dark energy, a0 = kappa c sqrt(G rho_DE) (kappa = 1/2, fitted), and a cold collisionless component (cold energy, Omega_c/Omega_b = 5.364) settles inside bound systems into the profile the law demands. The test is framework-native: the framework's own 1024^3 particle-mesh simulations (L = 100 Mpc/h) are scored, through the gravitating-field matter power spectrum, on the raw KiDS-1000 and DES Y3 shear correlation functions, against a same-pipeline control without settling; no LambdaCDM-calibrated nonlinear machinery enters the verdict.

The original settling rule (all baryons source the law; supply pooled across overlapping catchments) puts 19-25% too much power at k = 0.3-1 h/Mpc and is excluded (KiDS delta chi^2 = +68.7). A condensed-baryon census cap gives +14.0 (narrowly excluded). Two physically motivated rules - each halo settles only its own catchment's supply, and only condensed baryons (stars + cold gas) source the settled profile - bring the framework's boost to 1.005/1.012/1.023 at k = 0.3/0.5/1 and make KiDS-1000 consistent: delta chi^2 = +2.03 (robustness maximum +3.28; sensitivity tooth passes); absolute chi^2 146.3 (p = 0.011) vs the control's 144.3 (p = 0.014). DES Y3 is not diagnostic at this box size.

description:
Working note, version 1.0 (2026-10-15). AI-assisted research programme; not peer reviewed.

Cosmologically coupled black holes (CCBHs) have been proposed as the source of dark energy, with production tied to star formation and paid for by converting baryons (best fits leave ~70% of primordial baryons today; a conserved Madau-Dickinson history needs 57% removed). Fast radio bursts count the ionized baryons along each sightline. Fitting the mean cosmic dispersion-measure amplitude B to 114 localized FRBs (Sharma et al. 2026; authors' likelihood, host marginalised, scatter amplitude free) gives B = 1.064 [1.010, 1.122]. Baryon-only conversion is excluded at 7.8 sigma (s_b = 0.70) and 16.6 sigma (s_b = 0.43); with a 5% systematic floor the former stays at 5.6 sigma. Injection tests recover a planted deficit and separate B = 1 from B = 0.43 at 17 sigma in mocks. Pre-registered robustness tests (h, ionized-fraction model, host prior, BBN baryon density, sample, and all combined at worst) keep the exclusion at >= 5.1 sigma; one loophole - converted mass drawn entirely from the stellar channel under a doubled star-formation normalisation - lowers it to 2.5 sigma.

The same expansion history can instead be produced by converting the cold dark component, which is consistent with the FRBs (0.9 sigma): if black holes source dark energy, the converted mass must come mostly from the dark sector, not the baryons. We found no previous application of FRB dispersion measures to CCBH baryon depletion. Limitations: the Croker-like history uses the Madau-Dickinson shape; the mean model fixes the ionized fraction; gravitational-wave bounds independently disfavour k = 3. Scripts and frozen criteria: CFG779/CFG786 in the programme's public repository. AI assistance: Anthropic's Claude.

We describe configurations (source density swap preferred; distance change; combined), interleaved and blinded measurement, null checks, a precision budget, and the interpretation of each outcome. description:

We used the 3.5 m primary mirror of the Herschel Space Observatory as a dish antenna and archival HIFI band-1a heterodyne data as the receiver to search for a line at 541.664 GHz (m = 2.240 meV), the only vacuum-induced quantum mass of a gravity framework that ties the galactic acceleration scale to the dark-energy density (fitted coefficient kappa = 1/2). Because a mirror-generated line cancels in reference-subtracted archive spectra, we rebuilt total-power spectra from raw Level-0 counts against Herschel's internal hot and cold loads and stacked them in the spacecraft frame.

From 49 observations (7.0 h, 150 spectra) we find no line: a = -6.7 +- 7.7 mK (z = -0.86); 95% upper limit 12.7 mK, i.e. kinetic mixing epsilon < 1.9e-11 for a dish-coupling factor S = 50 (8.6e-12 to 8.6e-11 for S = 10-1000). The direct, cosmology-independent bound closes the window in which this field could be converted to light at useful efficiency (epsilon about 4-6e-9) by about 200x; it does not reach the framework's falsification level (about 1e-13). Note added in v1.1: a pre-registered follow-up (CFG802) traced the 3.2 sigma hint at 541.700 GHz to the instrument: it appears only in the H-polarisation receiver (z = +5.3 vs V -0.5) and is about 4 MHz wide rather than the 1.1 MHz instrument width (trials-corrected p = 0.08). It is not a line.

Two more days of pre-registered tests (criteria frozen before computing, mutation controls, post-hoc amendments disclosed, both a0 footings 9.36e-11 and 1.13e-10 m/s^2 reported and never pooled) of a gravity framework with galactic law g_N = g^2/(g + a0), a0 = (1/2) c sqrt(G rho_DE), whose extra gravitating mass is a collisionless 'cold energy' component, not a particle.

(1) Shear: rerun at 1024^3 from the framework's own early-universe inputs, the framework's particle-mesh structure is CONSISTENT with raw KiDS-1000 cosmic shear against its matched Poisson control on both footings (Delta chi^2 -10.08 canonical, -9.39 alternative); on the alternative footing DES Y3 is diagnostic and also CONSISTENT (-2.15). The size of the lead is amplitude-driven (KiDS Delta chi^2 -3.11 to -15.80 canonical and -2.93 to -14.69 alternative over the projection Omega_m; about -2.9 / -2.8 with the framework's own covariance), neither arm is a good absolute fit, and the engine that produces the pass has no established physical parent (companion note PAPER57): the pass is a computational result of that engine. (2) CMB lensing: on raw Planck PR4 lensing (L 8-400) all four runs are indistinguishable from their controls, CONSISTENT only under a post-hoc amendment, with little power; a sealed Fisher forecast finds that S4-class lensing at L ~ 1000-2000 could separate them. (3) The pressure-supported excess: dwarfs, spheroidal lenses and cluster cores carry an excess over the law and rotating systems do not, but no single kinematic measure, local density or any of five candidate selectors sets the amounts, and the record's own cold-energy equations cannot select on kinematics. The cluster-core excess is not a baryon-census error and survives four small reframings. A stellar-IMF correction removes the red-lens excess if discs are not bottom-heavy; the dwarf excess survives every reframing tried; a fossil a0 helps only under the rival a0 proportional to H(z), which is reported as evidence about a0(z), not as a rescue.

description:
Working note, version 1.0 (2026-10-21). AI-assisted research programme; not peer reviewed. kappa = 1/2 is fitted; the theory is not closed.

Structural lanes (criteria frozen before computing, mutation controls, post-hoc amendments disclosed, both a0 footings reported and never pooled) asking what any consistent theory of the collisionless 'cold energy' medium of a gravity framework must look like. The framework's galactic law is g_N = g^2/(g + a0), a0 = (1/2) c sqrt(G rho_DE); its extra gravitating mass is the cold energy, not a particle.

(1) A covariant parent: a fluid effective theory of comoving labels contains the record's static field equation under five stated conditions (CONDITIONAL). It reproduces the law to 2.2e-16 and has an isotropic dust background, a derived field-aligned stress, linear well-posedness and slip <= 1.54e-5. The medium's identity div P = rho - rhobar holds exactly through shell crossing, so the record's postulate that freed cold energy stays free cannot be derived from it. (2) No-go results: if the medium's excess is the law's phantom, the deep law forces the tether to cancel the medium's own gravity (no linear self-gravity, no gravity between tethered components). No ghost-free local Lagrangian switches the tether off in the linear universe without a vacuum offset 15-25 times the slip bound. A local second-order field that supplies the deep law must carry an external-field effect. Every tether without membership labels makes a satellite's medium hover while its stars fall. (3) No causal non-local parent has the record's cosmological engine as its exact limit: the engine's source relocation cannot conserve momentum, its resolution cut switches the law off for 128 of 175 SPARC galaxies, and its phantom is a global QUMOND field with an external-field effect. (4) Energy: the record's settling does not conserve energy, and no energy-conserving repair that keeps the released energy inside matter brings an infalling halo onto the law. (5) The labelled-domain construction removes the satellite hover and the linear-growth flag, but closes energy only through a non-dynamical label energy (NOT CONSISTENT AS SPECIFIED under its frozen rule; CONDITIONAL only under a post-hoc amendment), and it overshoots the eRASS1 cluster outer shear (Z = -9.3 canonical, -11.9 alternative). No complete parent survives. The two-footing shear pass of the companion notes remains a computational result of an engine whose physical parent is not established. (6) Data: faint gas-rich rotators do not reach the dwarfs' accelerations (not diagnostic); Coma ultra-diffuse galaxies sit above the derived ceiling, but not at 3 sigma once systematics are included; clusters modelled as untethered cold energy match the shear stack at the primary corner only, a fragile match.

Not derived: kappa = 1/2, the cold-to-baryon supply ratio, the retained fraction, the stiffness length. Companion notes: PAPER55 (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23482936) and PAPER56. AI assistance: Anthropic's Claude (analysis lanes, review, drafting).

description:
Working note, version 1.2 (2026-10-21; v1.1 and v1.0 2026-10-20; drafted 2026-10-14). AI-assisted research programme; not peer reviewed. kappa = 1/2 is fitted; the theory is not closed.

Correction (v1.1; wording fixed in v1.2): the exact static solution needs negative cold-energy density in a thin pancake through the saddle between two bodies (-89 times the mean cold density at R = 0.2 d for a Milky-Way-M31-like pair, -33 for a cluster pair, canonical footing). A medium of positive mass cannot supply this, so near field null points the cold energy must depart from the law. The total column through the saddle is still positive (negative part -0.206, net +0.016 in the solution's units), so neither picture predicts negative convergence there. Prediction: no saddle dip. Under the law the column through the saddle drops almost to zero in a narrow band; a positive medium cannot dig the part below zero density, a missing depth of 1.9 to 2.1 Msun/pc^2 (Milky-Way-M31-like pair) and 4.6 to 5.1 Msun/pc^2 (cluster pair). Published stacked lensing of luminous-red-galaxy pairs (arXiv:1702.08485) cannot test this yet (S/N below 1; about twelve times as many pairs needed). v1.1 called this "no negative lensing trough"; that wording was imprecise. The numbers are unchanged.

Galaxy rotation curves follow one relation between observed and baryonic acceleration, and in this framework its scale is set by dark energy, a0 = (1/2) c sqrt(G rho_DE). Clusters and the cosmic web also need a cold, collisionless mass component, 'cold energy', with Omega_c/Omega_b = 5.364 (measured). This short note explains why that component arranges itself, galaxy by galaxy, into exactly the profile the relation demands.

Cold energy is treated as a medium of real rest mass whose displacement P is the gravitational polarization. With K = 4 pi G and u = K|P|, the action is L = -|grad Phi - K P|^2/(2K) - rho_b Phi - W_rem(u) - (gamma/2)|grad P|^2, with K dW_rem/du = u^2/(a0 - u) and gamma = K L*^2/2. Varying Phi gives the baryons' Newtonian flux; varying P balances the baryons' inward pull g_N against the vacuum's push-back u^2/(a0 - u). The unique rest state is g_N = g^2/(g + a0), the simple interpolating function.

The stiffness length L* lies between 24 pc (set by Newtonian outer-halo globular clusters) and about 1 kpc. It screens the Solar System: Cassini's quadrupole is at most 5e-8 of the 2026 bound and the only residue is a uniform sunward pull of at most 2.4e-16 m/s^2. With catchment supply and condensed-only sourcing, the framework's own 1024^3 simulations are consistent with raw KiDS-1000 cosmic shear on both footings (Delta chi^2 -7.70 and -7.18 against a same-pipeline control) with inherited initial conditions; rerun with the framework's own initial conditions, the canonical footing still passes (Delta chi^2 -10.08), while the alternative-footing rerun is queued. An earlier own-supply rule is excluded by isolated-galaxy lensing, and an expelled-gas rule for hot-gas systems fails on the full 318 eRASS1 clusters.

Not derived: kappa = 1/2, Omega_c/Omega_b, L*, why only condensed baryons tether, and the relativistic completion. Sealed kill lines: a Cavendish test at four times the source acceleration (|dG/G| < 1e-6), a probe beyond 1000 AU (no non-thermal anomaly at or above 1e-13 m/s^2), and Gaia DR4 wide binaries (Newtonian). AI assistance: Anthropic's Claude, with review by parallel AI sessions.
title: Why Cold Energy Settles: A Tethered Medium Whose Displacement Is the Gravitational Polarization (Working Note)
